definition_zh: 同伴；伴侣；受雇陪护者；（成套物件中的）配对物；指南类书名用语
definition_en: a person who spends time with another, or one of a pair of matching things
core_image: 雪夜的山道上，两个旅人把同一块面包掰成两半，各自背着半袋干粮并排往前走
scene: 雪夜里，两个赶路的人分吃同一块面包，天亮时陌生人已经成了同行的人。The traveller shared his bread with a stranger at the pass, and by morning the stranger had become a companion.
sceneCN: 这里 companion 指「结伴同行、共处一段时间的人」（第 1 个义项：旅途或日常中与你同行的人）；句意为旅人在山口与陌生人分食面包，到天亮那人已成同伴。可辨识物件：雪夜、面包、行囊、提灯。

pos.zh: 同伴；伴侣；陪护者；（成套物件中的）配对物
陪伴（较少用，多见于书面）

collocations.zh: 形影不离的伙伴；长期相伴之物

senses.title: One who walks the road with you
senses.definition: a person who travels with you or shares a stretch of daily life
senses.definitionCN: 与你同行、共度一段日常生活的人
senses.example: She was his only companion on the six-week crossing.
senses.exampleCN: 在那次为期六周的横渡中，她是唯一的同伴。
senses.why: The Late Latin compound meant 'one who shares bread', and sharing bread on a journey is the oldest form of company.
senses.whyCN: 晚期拉丁的复合词意为「同吃面包的人」，而在旅途中分食面包正是最古老的作伴方式。

senses.title: Someone paid to stay beside a person
senses.titleCN: 受雇陪伴、照看他人的人
senses.definition: a person employed to live with or visit someone who needs company or care
senses.definitionCN: 受雇与需要陪伴或照看的人同住或定期探访的人
senses.example: The agency sends a companion three afternoons a week.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构每周派一名陪护来三个下午。
senses.why: The old sense of a person who stays beside another narrows into a paid role once families can buy the time they cannot give.
senses.whyCN: 「守在身旁的人」这一旧义，在家庭可以购买自己给不出的时间之后，收窄为一种受雇角色。

senses.title: A partner in a shared life
senses.definition: a person with whom one shares a long domestic life, without necessarily a legal tie
senses.definitionCN: 与之长期共同生活、未必有法律名分的人
senses.example: He introduced her simply as his companion of twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 他只说她是相伴二十年的伴侣。
senses.why: Staying beside someone is the core act, and the word lets that act stand without the labels of spouse or relation.
senses.whyCN: 守在身旁是这个词的核心动作，而这个词让这一动作无需配偶或亲属的名分也能成立。

senses.title: The matching half of a pair
senses.definition: one of two objects made to go together, especially the second of a set
senses.definitionCN: 成对制作、彼此配套的物件中的一件，尤指一套中的另一件
senses.example: The vase lost its companion in the move.
senses.exampleCN: 搬家时那只花瓶的配对件丢了。
senses.why: Once a person is seen as one of two who go together, the word transfers easily to objects that go together.
senses.whyCN: 当人被视为「成对同行」中的一方之后，这个词很容易移到成对出现的物件上。

senses.title: A book that travels with a text
senses.titleCN: 与某书配套的指南读物
senses.definition: a handbook designed to be read alongside a main work or a subject
senses.definitionCN: 与主书或某学科配套阅读的手册
senses.example: She bought a companion to the Greek myths before the course began.
senses.exampleCN: 课程开始前她买了一本希腊神话导读。
senses.why: A guide that sits beside a text does for the reader what a companion does for a traveller.
senses.whyCN: 一本陪在正文旁的指南对读者所做的事，正如同伴对旅人所做的事。

senses.title: A trait that goes with an experience
senses.titleCN: 与某种经历相伴而生的东西
senses.definition: something that regularly accompanies a condition or period
senses.definitionCN: 经常与某种状态或时期一同出现的事物
senses.example: Silence was the companion of those long laboratory nights.
senses.exampleCN: 那些漫长的实验之夜，总有沉默相伴。
senses.why: The abstract sense keeps the shape of two things travelling together but drops the human partner.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义保留了「两物同行」的形状，却去掉了人的那一方。

senses.title: A small body travelling with a larger one
senses.titleCN: 伴随大天体运行的小天体
senses.definition: a star or planet that orbits a larger body
senses.definitionCN: 绕较大天体运行的恒星或行星
senses.example: The telescope found a faint companion orbiting the distant star.
senses.exampleCN: 望远镜发现一颗暗弱伴星在绕那颗遥远恒星运行。
senses.why: Astronomy borrowed the everyday word because the two bodies really do travel together, one always beside the other.
senses.whyCN: 天文学借用了这个日常词，因为两个天体确实同行，一个始终在另一个旁边。

senses.title: A person attached to a household or order
senses.titleCN: 依附于某家、某团体的随从
senses.definition: a person attached to a household, an order or a cause in a subordinate role
senses.definitionCN: 以从属身份隶属于某家、某团体或某项事业的人
senses.example: The old chronicle lists the knight and his four companions.
senses.exampleCN: 那部旧编年史列出了这位骑士和他的四名随从。
senses.why: The medieval household kept companions as retainers, so the word once also meant a follower rather than an equal.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪的家庭以随从形式蓄养同伴，因此这个词一度也指追随者，而非平等者。

intro.en: Companion reached English through Old French compaignon from Late Latin companio, literally 'one who shares bread', built on com- 'together' and panis 'bread'. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: companion 经古法语 compaignon 来自晚期拉丁 companio，字面为「同吃面包的人」，由 com-「共同」与 panis「面包」构成。下列年代均为约数。

items.en: Panis 'bread' is a well-recorded Latin noun. Its deeper origin is not settled; the link sometimes suggested to a root meaning 'to feed' is a hypothesis, and any Indo-European form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: panis「面包」是有充分记录的拉丁名词。其更深来源未有定论；有人把它与表示「喂养」的词根联系起来，那只是假说，凡为其给出的印欧形式均属重构形式。

items.en: The prefix com-, a form of cum 'with', assimilates to the consonant that follows it and appears as com- before p. It adds the sense of doing something together.
items.cn: 前缀 com- 是 cum「与」的变体，会随后面的辅音同化，在 p 前写作 com-；它增添「一同做某事」的意思。

items.en: Companio is recorded in late texts for a messmate, one who shares bread. The compound itself is documented, but only in late sources, so no earlier first date can be confirmed.
items.cn: companio 见于晚期文献，指同席吃饭、分食面包的人。这一复合词本身有书证，但只见于晚期材料，更早的首见年代无法确认。

items.en: Old French compaignon passed into Middle English in the thirteenth century, first naming a fellow soldier or a close associate and later any person who keeps one company.
items.cn: 古法语 compaignon 在十三世纪进入中古英语，最初指同袍或亲密伙伴，后来泛指任何作伴的人。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the earliest English citation is not fixed with confidence, and the pre-Latin origin of panis is unsettled, so any deeper root offered for it is only a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：最早的英语书证无法确定年份；panis 在拉丁语之前的来源亦无定论，凡为其给出的更深词根都只是重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same bread compound or close to it in shape; group two holds the people and things that actually keep you company.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「面包」复合词或字形相近的词；第二组是真正陪你作伴的人与物。

entries.definition: From the same Late Latin companio, but it names a group rather than one person, and later also a business firm.
entries.definitionCN: 同出晚期拉丁的 companio，但它指一群人，而不是一个人，后来又指一家公司。

entries.definition: The verb built on the same Old French stem; it is the act of going along with someone, not the person who goes.
entries.definitionCN: 这个动词由同一古法语词干构成；它指陪同这一动作，而不是陪同的人。

entries.definition: Com- plus pati 'to suffer': sorrow felt for someone's suffering, with neither bread nor companionship in its root.
entries.definitionCN: com- 加 pati「受苦」：为他人苦难而生的悲悯，词根里既没有面包，也没有陪伴。

entries.definition: Com- plus patria 'fatherland': a fellow citizen, so the second element is a country, not bread.
entries.definitionCN: com- 加 patria「祖国」：指同国之人，第二个成分是国土，不是面包。

entries.definition: A person who shares an activity, a business or a life on equal terms; it is more formal than companion and usually implies a defined role.
entries.definitionCN: 在活动、事业或生活上以平等身份共处的人；比 companion 正式，通常含明确的角色。

entries.definition: An informal word for a friend or a pair-member, common in British speech and among animals.
entries.definitionCN: 指朋友或配对成员的通俗词，在英式口语与动物身上都常见。

entries.definition: A person who accompanies someone for protection or as an attendant; the going-with is a service, not a bond.
entries.definitionCN: 为保护或礼仪而陪同的人；这种陪同是一种服务，而非情感联系。

entries.definition: A person or state joined to another for a shared purpose; the link is strategic, while a companion is personal.
entries.definitionCN: 为共同目的而与另一方联合的人或国家；这种联结是策略性的，而同伴是私人性的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin bread word, the real household of words built on it, and the real phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实存在的拉丁「面包」词、由它构成的真实词族，以及这个词真实出现的搭配。

normal.en: The Late Latin compound means 'bread-sharer', so a companion is the person you break bread with.
normal.cn: 晚期拉丁的复合词意为「分食面包者」，所以同伴就是与你掰开同一块面包的人。

normal.en: The same stem yields company, a group, and accompany, to go with; the whole family points to going along together.
normal.cn: 同一词干衍生出 company（一群人）与 accompany（陪同），整个词族都指向「一同前行」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the shades: travel companion, constant companion, companion volume.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出不同侧重：旅伴、形影不离的伙伴、配套卷册。

normal.en: The suffix -ship turns the person into the relationship, giving companionship, the state of having such a person.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ship 把人变成关系，构成 companionship，即「有这样一个人在身边」的状态。

normal.en: Bread turns up again in pantry, which also descends from panis through Old French.
normal.cn: 「面包」这个词还出现在 pantry 中，它同样经古法语来自 panis。

abstract.en: Picture one loaf cut in half on a stone table, with two knives and one lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象一只面包在石桌上被切成两半，旁边放着两把刀和一盏灯。

abstract.en: Picture a walk where neither person has to explain why the other is still there.
abstract.cn: 想象一段路，两个人都无需解释对方为何还在。

abstract.en: Picture a small dark star circling a bright one, never seen directly, only deduced.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗暗小的星绕着亮星转，从未被直接看到，只靠推算得知。

examples.en: For three days the injured climber's only companion was a radio.
examples.cn: 整整三天，受伤登山者唯一的同伴是一台收音机。

examples.en: The exhibition pairs each painting with a companion sketch from the same year.
examples.cn: 展览为每幅画配上一张同年的草图。

examples.en: Astronomers measured the pull of a companion too faint to be seen.
examples.cn: 天文学家测出了一颗暗到看不见的伴星的引力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「com（共同）+ pan（面包）」——同吃一块面包的人 → 同伴、伴侣

root: 晚期拉丁 companio「同吃面包的人」= com-（共同）+ panis（面包）；panis 更深来源不确定，其印欧祖形仅为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one loaf: bread shared on a road becomes a fellow traveller, a paid presence, a life partner, the matching half of a set, a book that travels beside a text, a mood that travels with a period, and finally a faint star that travels with a bright one.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一只面包展开：路上分食面包的人，先是旅伴，再是受雇的陪护、共同生活的伴侣，随后是成套物件中的另一半、陪在正文旁的指南、与某段日子同行的心境，最后是伴着亮星运行的一颗暗星。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a loaf broken in two on a road, and the two halves kept moving in step.
core.cn: 核心意象：路上掰成两半的一只面包，两半始终同一步伐向前。

branches.en: TRAVEL AND CARE: a bread-sharer on the road, then someone paid to stay beside a person who should not be alone.
branches.cn: 同行与照看：先是路上的分食者，再是受雇守在不宜独处之人身旁的人。

branches.en: SHARED LIFE: the staying-beside made permanent and personal rather than paid or formal.
branches.cn: 共同生活：把「守在身旁」变成长期而私人的事，既不付酬，也不拘名分。

branches.en: MATCHED HALF: the word leaves people behind and names the second of two objects that belong together.
branches.cn: 配成一对：这个词离开人，转而指两件应当配在一起的物件中的另一件。

branches.en: PRINTED AND SERVING: a book that goes beside a text, and a retainer who goes beside a household.
branches.cn: 纸页与随从：陪在正文旁的书，以及跟在家族身边的从属者。

branches.en: TRAIT AND STAR: something that always travels with an experience, and a faint body that travels with a bright one.
branches.cn: 伴随物与天体：总是与某段经历同行的心境，以及紧随亮星运行的小天体。

intro.en: Companion can be read morpheme by morpheme, because both the prefix and the bread word still build other English words.
intro.cn: companion 可以按语素逐个读出，因为它的前缀与「面包」那一部分都还在构成其他英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin panis gives companion, company, accompany and pantry; the prefix com- adds the sense of doing something together.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 panis 衍生 companion、company、accompany 与 pantry；前缀 com- 增添「一同做某事」的意思。

items.example: The prefix binds two people into one shared act.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把两个人收束进同一个动作。

items.example: The root supplies the food that is shared.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供被分食的那种食物。

items.example: The late compound named a messmate before it named a friend.
items.exampleCN: 这个晚期复合词先指同席者，后指朋友。

items.example: The traveller's companion carried half the food.
items.exampleCN: 旅人的同伴背着半份干粮。

items.meaning: the state of having a companion
items.example: Her companionship made the long winter bearable.
items.exampleCN: 她的陪伴让漫长的冬天可以忍受。

items.example: He is quiet but companionable on long walks.
items.exampleCN: 他话不多，却适合一起长途散步。

items.example: The last years left him almost companionless.
items.exampleCN: 最后几年他几乎无人作伴。

items.structure: ac- (form of ad- 'to') + the same Old French stem
items.example: Two nurses accompany the patient to the theatre.
items.exampleCN: 两名护士陪同病人去手术室。

items.meaningCN: 一同进食的一群人；公司
items.example: The whole company sat down at one long table.
items.exampleCN: 全公司的人坐在一张长桌旁。

latinEntries.structure: companio, companionis (m., third declension, Late Latin)

definition_zh: 友谊；朋友关系；友情；（团体、国家间的）友好关系
definition_en: the relationship between friends, based on mutual trust and goodwill
core_image: 两个孩子在院墙两边埋下同一颗种子，藤蔓翻过墙头缠在一起，谁也没有去剪断
scene: 两个邻村的少年各走一半的路，在界石旁交换午饭，谁也不欠谁。The two boys from rival villages met at the boundary stone each day and shared their lunches, and that friendship outlasted the quarrel between their families.
sceneCN: 这里 friendship 指「朋友之间彼此信任、互相往来的关系」（第 1 个义项：平等者之间长期自愿的友好关系）；句意为两个敌对村庄的少年每天在界石旁分吃午饭，这份友情比两家人的争吵更长久。可辨识物件：界石、饭盒、半旧书包、田埂。

pos.zh: 友谊；朋友关系；友情；（团体间的）友好关系

senses.title: A bond two people keep choosing
senses.titleCN: 两人自愿维持的长期情谊
senses.definition: the warm, trusting relationship between people who choose each other's company
senses.definitionCN: 彼此选择对方作伴、相互信任的温暖关系
senses.example: Their friendship began in a shared dormitory and lasted fifty years.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的友谊始于同一间宿舍，持续了五十年。
senses.why: Old English built the word from friend plus -ship, a suffix for a state, so friendship is simply the condition of being friends.
senses.whyCN: 古英语用 friend 加表示状态的后缀构成这个词，因此友谊就是「作为朋友」的那种状态。

senses.title: The goodwill a friend carries
senses.definition: the affectionate goodwill that a friend feels and shows
senses.definitionCN: 朋友所怀有并表现出来的亲切善意
senses.example: He spoke of her with real friendship, not mere politeness.
senses.exampleCN: 他谈到她时带着真正的友情，而不只是客套。
senses.why: If friendship is a state, it can also be the feeling that maintains it, so the word names the warmth as well as the relation.
senses.whyCN: 如果说友谊是一种状态，它也可以指维持这种状态的情感，因此这个词既指关系，也指那份温情。

senses.title: The years a friendship lasts
senses.definition: the condition of being friends over a particular stretch of time
senses.definitionCN: 在某一特定时段内保持朋友关系的情形
senses.example: The friendship cooled after the business dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 那场生意纠纷之后，这份友谊冷了下来。
senses.why: The same noun covers the bond and its lifetime, since a relationship exists only as long as it is kept up.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词既指情谊，也指它的存续期，因为关系只在被维持的期间内存在。

senses.title: Goodwill between groups or states
senses.titleCN: 团体或国家之间的友好关系
senses.definition: a cooperative relationship between organizations or countries that are not formally allied
senses.definitionCN: 未正式结盟的组织或国家之间的合作关系
senses.example: The two cities signed a friendship agreement in the town hall.
senses.exampleCN: 两座城市在市政厅签署了友好协议。
senses.why: Cities and states borrow the personal word for a link that is warmer than a treaty but less binding than an alliance.
senses.whyCN: 城市与国家借用这个私人词，指一种比条约更温和、比同盟更松散的联结。

senses.title: One friendship among many
senses.definition: a single instance of such a bond, countable and distinct from the rest
senses.definitionCN: 这种关系的一次具体实例，可数且与其余各段相区别
senses.example: She kept up friendships from every decade of her life.
senses.exampleCN: 她与人生每个十年里结识的朋友都保持着往来。
senses.why: Counting the word separates one particular bond from the general virtue, which is why the plural is so common.
senses.whyCN: 把词变成可数，就把某一段具体情谊与作为美德的友谊区分开来，因此复数形式极为常见。

senses.title: A link accepted on a screen
senses.titleCN: 社交平台上接受的好友关系
senses.definition: a connection accepted on a social platform that presents two users as friends
senses.definitionCN: 在社交平台上被接受、把两名用户呈现为好友的联结
senses.example: He accepted the friendship without ever meeting the man.
senses.exampleCN: 他接受了那条好友请求，却从未见过对方。
senses.why: Platforms needed a noun for the link itself, so they reused the oldest word for a bond and emptied it of time and trust.
senses.whyCN: 平台需要为这种联结找一个名词，于是动用了表示情谊的最古老的词，却抽掉了时间与信任。

senses.title: An alliance kept for advantage
senses.definition: a friendly arrangement maintained for gain rather than affection
senses.definitionCN: 出于得益而非情意维持的友好安排
senses.example: Their friendship was a friendship of convenience and both knew it.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的友情是彼此方便的结交，两边都心知肚明。
senses.why: Because the word promises trust, it can also be used ironically for a link that merely looks like trust.
senses.whyCN: 正因为这个词许诺信任，它也能反用来指一种只是看起来像信任的联结。

senses.title: Friendship as a thing to study
senses.titleCN: 被当作研究对象或德性的友谊
senses.definition: the virtue or social institution that philosophers and sociologists examine
senses.definitionCN: 哲学家与社会学家所考察的德性或社会制度
senses.example: The course reads ancient letters as evidence of how friendship was understood.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课把古代书信当作理解当时友谊观念的证据。
senses.why: Once a word names a relation, it can also name the thing itself as a topic, which is how friendship became a subject with a literature.
senses.whyCN: 一个词一旦指称某种关系，也能指称作为题目的事物本身，友谊由此成为有文献可查的课题。

intro.en: Friendship is an Old English compound of freond 'friend' and -scipe 'state, condition'. The noun for friend began as a participle of a verb meaning 'to love, to favour'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: friendship 是古英语复合词，由 freond「朋友」与 -scipe「状态、身份」构成。friend 最初是表示「爱、眷顾」的动词的分词。下列年代均为约数。

items.en: Freond 'friend' continues a Germanic participle meaning 'loving, favouring', from a verb reconstructed as frijon 'to love'. The verb form is a reconstruction, not a recorded word.
items.cn: freond「朋友」承自一个意为「爱着、眷顾着」的日耳曼语分词，其动词被重构为 frijon「爱」；该动词形式属重构，并非有记录的词。

items.en: -scipe meant 'state, condition, office' and is the same suffix heard in lordship and hardship; it names what a person or thing is, not what they do.
items.cn: -scipe 意为「状态、身份、职位」，与 lordship、hardship 中的后缀相同；它指人或物「是什么」，而非「做什么」。

items.en: The compound is recorded in Old English for friendship or favour, but no single earliest citation can be dated precisely.
items.cn: 这一复合词在古英语中已用来指友谊或眷顾，但没有哪一条最早书证能定出确切年代。

items.en: Middle English carried the word through changes of spelling without changing its sense, and it remained the ordinary noun for the bond between friends.
items.cn: 中古英语在拼写变化中沿用这个词，词义未变，它始终是表示朋友间情谊的常用名词。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root and first date): the Germanic verb behind friend is reconstructed, its Indo-European ancestor is likewise a reconstruction, and the earliest Old English citation is not fixed with confidence.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根与首见年代）：friend 背后的日耳曼语动词属重构，其印欧祖形同样是重构，古英语最早书证也无法确定年份。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root family and one near neighbour of a different root that is often mistaken for a relative; group two holds the words that describe closeness between people.
note.cn: 第一组是同根词族，外加一个常被误认作同族、实则不同源的近形词；第二组是描述人际亲近的近似词。

entries.definition: The noun inside the compound; it names the person, while friendship names the relationship between two such people.
entries.definitionCN: 复合词中的名词部分；它指人，而 friendship 指两个这样的人之间的关系。

entries.definition: The adjective built on friend with the old suffix for 'having the form of'; it describes behaviour, not the bond itself.
entries.definitionCN: 由 friend 加表示「具有……形态」的旧后缀构成的形容词；它描述行为，而非关系本身。

entries.definition: Old English feond meant 'enemy'; the shape is close to friend but the roots are unrelated, which is why the pair is a trap.
entries.definitionCN: 古英语 feond 意为「敌人」；字形与 friend 相近，词根却毫无关系，因此这一对极易误认。

entries.definition: Un- plus friend, formed in the age of social platforms for removing a name from a list; it is not an old word.
entries.definitionCN: 由 un- 加 friend，在社交平台时代才出现，指把某人移出好友名单；它不是古老词。

entries.definition: The state of having someone beside you; it stresses presence and shared hours rather than the affection friendship implies.
entries.definitionCN: 身边有人的状态；它强调在场与共处的时间，而非 friendship 所含的情意。

entries.definition: The closeness of people who work or fight together; it rests on a common task, while friendship rests on choice.
entries.definitionCN: 一同工作或战斗的人之间的亲近；它依托共同任务，而友谊依托彼此选择。

entries.definition: Any strong link between people, including family and colleagues; it is broader and often more physical in feel.
entries.definitionCN: 人与人之间的任何强烈联结，包括家人与同事；含义更宽，感觉上常更具体。

entries.definition: A formal union of parties for a purpose; it is political or strategic, and carries none of the warmth of friendship.
entries.definitionCN: 各方为某目的结成的正式联合；它是政治或策略性的，不含友谊的温情。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Old English parts, the real suffix family and the real verbs that pair with the noun.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实存在的古英语构词成分、真实的后缀词族，以及真实与这个名词搭配的动词。

normal.en: The suffix is the one heard in lordship and hardship: a state or condition, here the state of being a friend.
normal.cn: 这个后缀也出现在 lordship 与 hardship 中：表状态或身份，此处即「身为朋友」的状态。

normal.en: Friend began as a participle meaning 'loving', so friendship is literally the condition of one who loves.
normal.cn: friend 原为意为「爱着」的分词，所以友谊字面上就是「爱着的人所处的状态」。

normal.en: The noun takes real verbs: form a friendship, strike up a friendship, keep up a friendship, break off a friendship.
normal.cn: 这个名词有真实动词搭配：建立友谊、结下友谊、维持友谊、断绝友谊。

normal.en: Its adjective is friendly and its abstract quality is friendliness, both built with ordinary English endings.
normal.cn: 它的形容词是 friendly，抽象性质是 friendliness，两者都用普通英语词尾构成。

normal.en: Companionship is the nearest rival, but it counts hours together, while friendship counts affection.
normal.cn: 最接近的是 companionship，但它算的是共处的时间，而 friendship 算的是情意。

abstract.en: Picture a vine crossing a wall because two children planted the same seed on both sides.
abstract.cn: 想象一株藤蔓翻过院墙，因为两个孩子在墙两边种下了同一颗种子。

abstract.en: Picture two chairs left outside overnight, neither moved, both damp with the same rain.
abstract.cn: 想象两把椅子整夜放在户外，谁也没搬动，被同一场雨同时打湿。

abstract.en: Picture a debt between two people that neither of them ever tries to settle.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人之间的一笔账，谁也从不去结清。

examples.en: Their friendship survived a year of silence and two arguments about money.
examples.cn: 他们的友谊熬过了一年的沉默与两次关于钱的争吵。

examples.en: The school pairs older pupils with younger ones to build friendships across year groups.
examples.cn: 学校让高年级学生与低年级学生结对，以跨年级建立友谊。

examples.en: The two ports have kept a friendship agreement since the war ended.
examples.cn: 战争结束后，两座港口城市一直维持着友好协议。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「friend（朋友）+ ship（船）」——同坐一条船的朋友 → 友谊

root: 古英语 freond「朋友」+ -scipe「状态、身份」；freond 原为「爱、眷顾」动词的分词，该日耳曼语动词与印欧祖形均属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one chosen bond: two people keep choosing each other, the goodwill they carry, the years it lasts, the goodwill between cities, single instances of it, a link accepted on a screen, a bargain dressed as affection, and the thing philosophers study.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一份自愿的情谊展开：两人不断重新选择对方、心中所怀的善意、情谊存续的岁月、城市之间的友好、若干段中的一段、屏幕上接受的联结、披着情意的利益结交，最后是被当作课题来研究的友谊。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a vine grown from one seed on two sides of a wall, never cut where it crosses.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗种子在墙两边长出的同一株藤，越过墙头处从未被剪断。

branches.en: PERSONAL BOND IN TIME: the relationship itself and the stretch of years through which it is kept up.
branches.cn: 私人情谊及其岁月：关系本身，以及维持这段关系的那些年头。

branches.en: THE FEELING INSIDE IT: goodwill is what keeps the state alive from day to day.
branches.cn: 关系中的情感：善意是让这种状态逐日存活的东西。

branches.en: BETWEEN BODIES: cities and states borrow the personal word for cooperation without a treaty.
branches.cn: 团体之间：城市与国家借用这个私人词，指不签条约的合作。

branches.en: COUNTED AND BARGAINED: one friendship among many, and the ironic version kept only for advantage.
branches.cn: 可数者与交易者：若干段中的一段，以及只为利益而维持的那种反用。

branches.en: SCREEN AND STUDY: a link emptied of time, and the bond turned into a subject with a literature.
branches.cn: 屏幕与学问：被抽掉时间的联结，以及成为有文献之课题的情谊。

intro.en: Friendship is a Germanic compound whose two parts still work separately in English, so the whole family reads clearly.
intro.cn: friendship 是日耳曼语复合词，两部分在英语中仍各自独立运作，因此整个词族都能读得清楚。

latinIntro.en: The word has no Latin root: friend and -ship are both Germanic, and the suffix is still productive in modern English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根：friend 与 -ship 都属日耳曼语，而这个后缀在现代英语中仍有构词能力。

items.example: The first element names the person who loves.
items.exampleCN: 第一个成分指怀着爱意的那个人。

items.example: The suffix turns a person into a relationship.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把人变成一种关系。

items.example: Their friendship lasted fifty years.
items.exampleCN: 他们的友谊持续了五十年。

items.example: The new neighbour was friendly from the first morning.
items.exampleCN: 新邻居从第一个早晨就很友善。

items.example: Her friendliness made the office easier to enter.
items.exampleCN: 她的友善让这间办公室更容易走进。

items.meaning: to act as a friend toward someone
items.example: A retired teacher befriended the boy.
items.exampleCN: 一位退休教师与那男孩结为朋友。

items.meaning: to remove someone from a list of friends
items.example: He unfriended her after the argument.
items.exampleCN: 争吵之后他把她删除了好友。

items.example: The first term left him friendless in a new city.
items.exampleCN: 第一个学期让他在新城市里没有朋友。

definition_zh: 友好的；亲切的；（关系）和睦的；（设备、政策）便于使用的；非正式比赛的；友军的
definition_en: kind and pleasant toward others, or designed to cause no difficulty
core_image: 清晨的院门口，主人把门闩拉开一半，站在门边等人走近，狗也没有叫
scene: 搬来第一天，隔壁的老人端着一盘刚烙的饼站在门口，狗摇着尾巴没有叫。The old woman next door came out with a plate of warm flatbread, and even the dog was friendly.
sceneCN: 这里 friendly 指「待人亲切、使人感到不受排斥」（第 1 个义项：对人温和有礼、乐于接近）；句意为隔壁老人端着热饼出来，连狗都很友善。可辨识物件：门槛、热饼、盘子、摇尾的狗。

pos.zh: 友好的；亲切的；和睦的；便于使用的；非正式的；友方的

derivatives.zh: 朋友（形容词的基础名词）

senses.title: Kind in the way you treat people
senses.definition: behaving in a warm and helpful way toward other people
senses.definitionCN: 以温和、乐于相助的方式对待他人
senses.example: The new neighbour was friendly from the first morning.
senses.exampleCN: 新邻居从第一个早晨就很亲切。
senses.why: The Old English adjective was built from friend plus a suffix meaning 'having the form of', so being friendly is literally looking and acting like a friend.
senses.whyCN: 这个古英语形容词由 friend 加表示「具有……形态」的后缀构成，因此友好字面上就是「像朋友那样待人」。

senses.title: Warm in appearance or atmosphere
senses.definition: looking welcoming rather than cold, formal or forbidding
senses.definitionCN: 看上去令人愿意走近，而非冷淡、拘谨或拒人于外
senses.example: The café had a friendly clutter of books and mugs.
senses.exampleCN: 那家咖啡馆堆着书和杯子，显得亲切随意。
senses.why: If a person can look like a friend, so can a room, and the adjective transfers to places that make people feel accepted.
senses.whyCN: 既然人可以看起来像朋友，房间也可以，于是这个形容词扩展到让人感到被接纳的场所。

senses.title: Cooperative between groups
senses.titleCN: 团体或国家之间和睦合作
senses.definition: not hostile and willing to work with another group or country
senses.definitionCN: 不怀敌意，愿意与另一团体或国家合作
senses.example: The two ports kept friendly relations through the dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 争端期间，两座港口城市仍保持友好关系。
senses.why: States borrow the personal adjective for relations that are peaceful without being formally allied.
senses.whyCN: 国家借用这个私人形容词，指和平共处但未正式结盟的关系。

senses.title: Easy to use or live with
senses.definition: designed or arranged so that it gives the user no trouble
senses.definitionCN: 经过设计或安排，使用起来不添麻烦
senses.example: The guide is written in friendly language for beginners.
senses.exampleCN: 这本指南用初学者也能亲近的语言写成。
senses.why: The modern sense takes the warmth of a helpful person and applies it to machines and policies that behave as if they wanted to help.
senses.whyCN: 现代义把助人者的温和，移用到那些表现得仿佛愿意帮忙的机器与政策上。

senses.title: Well disposed toward a plan
senses.definition: showing support or sympathy toward an idea, cause or proposal
senses.definitionCN: 对某个想法、事业或提议表示支持或同情
senses.example: The council was friendly to the idea of a night bus.
senses.exampleCN: 市议会对开设夜班公交的想法持赞许态度。
senses.why: Being friendly to a proposal is the political version of being friendly to a person: no hostility, an open door.
senses.whyCN: 对一项提议友好，是对人友好的政治版本：无敌意，门是开的。

senses.title: Sociable by nature, of animals
senses.definition: of an animal, inclined to approach people rather than avoid them
senses.definitionCN: 指动物愿意接近人而不是躲避人
senses.example: Their dog is friendly with every child on the street.
senses.exampleCN: 他们家的狗对街上每个孩子都很亲。
senses.why: The word describes temperament as well as behaviour, so an animal that seeks company is called friendly even when nobody is present.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既描述行为也描述性情，因此愿意亲近人的动物即使无人在场也被称为 friendly。

senses.title: Not counting toward a result
senses.definition: arranged for practice or goodwill rather than for a competitive result
senses.definitionCN: 为练习或友好而安排，不以竞赛结果为重
senses.example: They played a friendly before the league began.
senses.exampleCN: 联赛开始前他们踢了一场友谊赛。
senses.why: A match played in the spirit of friends is one whose score does not matter, so the adjective marks the absence of stakes.
senses.whyCN: 以朋友之道进行的比赛，比分并不重要，因此这个形容词标示「无关利害」。

senses.title: Of one's own side, by accident
senses.definition: belonging to one's own forces, used of accidental damage caused by them
senses.definitionCN: 属于己方部队，用于指己方造成的误伤
senses.example: Friendly fire damaged two of their own trucks.
senses.exampleCN: 友军火力误伤了他们自己的两辆卡车。
senses.why: The cruel irony is that fire from friends is still called friendly; the adjective marks the side, not the kindness.
senses.whyCN: 残酷的反讽在于，来自同伴的火力仍被称作「友方的」；这个形容词标的是阵营，不是善意。

intro.en: Friendly is an Old English adjective, freondlic, from freond 'friend' and -lic 'having the form or body of'. That suffix survives as modern -ly. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: friendly 是古英语形容词 freondlic，由 freond「朋友」与 -lic「具有……形态或形体」构成。这个后缀在现代英语中写作 -ly。下列年代均为约数。

items.en: The suffix -lic meant 'having the body or form of' and is the source of modern -ly; the adjective and the adverb both grew from it, which is why the two forms look alike.
items.cn: 后缀 -lic 意为「具有……形体或形态」，是现代 -ly 的来源；形容词与副词都由它生长出来，因此两种形式看起来一样。

items.en: Freondlic joined the noun for friend with that suffix to mean 'like a friend, kindly'. The compound is recorded in Old English, though no earliest citation can be dated exactly.
items.cn: freondlic 把表示朋友的名词与该后缀结合，意为「像朋友一样的、厚道的」。这一复合词在古英语中有书证，但最早一条无法定出确切年代。

items.en: Middle English kept the adjective and also formed a matching adverb from the same ending; the two were not separately invented, they simply parted company in use.
items.cn: 中古英语保留了这个形容词，同时用同一词尾构成对应的副词；两者并非各自新造，只是在用法上分了家。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the adjective was attached to nouns to mean 'causing no harm or difficulty', producing forms such as user-friendly and environment-friendly.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，这个形容词被接到名词前，表示「不造成伤害或麻烦」，于是出现「对使用者友好」「对环境友好」这类说法。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest recorded use of the Old English adjective cannot be dated with confidence, and the exact relation between the adjective and the adverb in early Middle English is still argued; the Germanic root behind friend is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：古英语形容词最早的书证无法确定年份；中古英语早期形容词与副词的确切关系仍有争论；friend 背后的日耳曼语词根属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root family plus one near neighbour with an unrelated root; group two holds adjectives that describe a pleasant manner.
note.cn: 第一组是同根词族，外加一个字形相近却不同源的词；第二组是描述待人态度令人舒服的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun underneath the adjective; a friendly act is one a friend might do, while a friend is the person himself.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词底下的名词；friendly 的行为是朋友会做的事，而 friend 是那个人本身。

entries.definition: The quality formed with -ness; the adjective describes one act or mood, the noun names the lasting trait.
entries.definitionCN: 由 -ness 构成的品质名词；形容词描述一次行为或一时心境，名词指长期的性情。

entries.definition: Old English feond 'enemy'; nearly the same shape as friend, but there is no shared root, so the resemblance is a trap.
entries.definitionCN: 古英语 feond「敌人」；字形与 friend 几乎相同，词根却毫无关系，这种相似是个陷阱。

entries.definition: Un- plus friendly; it negates the manner but not necessarily the whole person, since a friendly person can have an unfriendly day.
entries.definitionCN: un- 加 friendly；它否定的是举止，不一定是整个人，因为一个友善的人也会有不友善的一天。

entries.definition: Formal and slightly old-fashioned: easy to like and pleasant to be with, describing disposition more than action.
entries.definitionCN: 正式且略显陈旧：讨人喜欢、相处舒服，更多描述性情而非具体行为。

entries.definition: Warm and sincere in a restrained, often official way, as in a cordial welcome; it is cooler than friendly in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 以克制、常带官方色彩的方式表达热情真诚，如「诚挚的欢迎」；语气比 friendly 更冷静。

entries.definition: Inclined to mix with others and enjoy their company; it describes the appetite for company rather than the treatment of it.
entries.definitionCN: 喜欢与人交往并享受共处；它描述对人群的喜好，而不是对待他人的方式。

entries.definition: Actively making a newcomer feel wanted; it focuses on the first moment of arrival, where friendly can describe a long habit.
entries.definitionCN: 主动让新来者感到被欢迎；它着眼于刚到场的那一刻，而 friendly 可以指长期的习惯。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real suffix history, the real compounds and the real pairings of the word.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的后缀演变、真实的复合词，以及这个词真实的搭配。

normal.en: The same ending that gives friendly also gives the adverb -ly, so the adjective and the adverb share one suffix.
normal.cn: 构成 friendly 的词尾同时也构成副词后缀 -ly，形容词与副词共用一个来源。

normal.en: Modern compounds are transparent: friendly to users, friendly to the environment, friendly to families.
normal.cn: 现代复合词一目了然：便于使用的、对环境友好的、适合家庭观看的。

normal.en: The word pairs with relations, atmosphere and terms: friendly relations, a friendly atmosphere, on friendly terms.
normal.cn: 这个词常与关系、气氛、相处状态搭配：友好关系、亲切气氛、关系和睦。

normal.en: Its opposite is simply unfriendly, with no separate root to learn.
normal.cn: 它的反义词只是加 un-，不必另记词根。

normal.en: In sport a friendly is a match whose result does not count, which is why the adjective can mean 'without stakes'.
normal.cn: 在体育中，friendly 指不计成绩的比赛，这解释了形容词为何能表示「无关利害」。

abstract.en: Picture a door left half open with a lamp still on behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门半开着，门后还亮着灯。

abstract.en: Picture a dog that wags instead of barks when a stranger reaches the gate.
abstract.cn: 想象陌生人走到门口时，狗摇尾巴而不是叫。

abstract.en: Picture a machine whose buttons are labelled in the order you would actually want to press them.
abstract.cn: 想象一台机器，按钮的排列正是你真正想按的顺序。

examples.en: A friendly librarian found him a desk when every seat was taken.
examples.cn: 所有座位都满了，一位友善的馆员还是给他找到一张桌子。

examples.en: The two committees have stayed friendly even when they disagreed.
examples.cn: 两个委员会即使意见相左，也一直保持友好。

examples.en: The village is not exactly beautiful, but it is friendly.
examples.cn: 这个村子算不上美，但待人亲切。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「friend（朋友）+ ly」——像朋友一样待人 → 友好的

root: 古英语 freond「朋友」+ -lic（「具有……形态」，今为 -ly）；friend 背后的日耳曼语词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: a door left open. It starts with a person, moves to a room, then to relations between ports, then to tools and policies that behave as if they wanted to help, then to a friendly stance, a friendly animal, a match without stakes, and finally to fire from your own side.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一个动作展开：一扇留开的门。它从一个人开始，移到一间屋子，再移到港口之间的关系，又移到那些仿佛愿意帮忙的工具与政策，然后是赞许的态度、亲人的动物、不计输赢的比赛，最后是来自己方的火力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door held half open, with a lamp behind it and no lock in sight.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇半开的门，门后有灯，看不见锁。

branches.en: PERSON THEN PLACE: a person treats you like a friend, and then a room is arranged to feel the same.
branches.cn: 先人后屋：先是一个人把你当朋友对待，然后是一间屋子被布置成同样的感觉。

branches.en: PEACE WITHOUT STAKES: friendly relations between ports, and a match arranged so the score does not matter.
branches.cn: 不计利害的和睦：港口之间的友好关系，以及一场比分无关紧要的比赛。

branches.en: DESIGNED TO HELP: machines and policies that act as if they wanted to make your way easier.
branches.cn: 为人省事的设计：那些表现得仿佛愿意替你省力的机器与政策。

branches.en: AN OPEN STANCE: approval toward a proposal, and an animal that comes toward people rather than away.
branches.cn: 开放的姿态：对提议的赞许，以及主动靠近人而非躲开的动物。

branches.en: THE IRONIC SIDE: fire from your own side is still called friendly, because the word marks the camp and not the kindness.
branches.cn: 反讽的阵营：来自己方的火力仍被称作「友方的」，因为这个形容词标的是阵营，不是善意。

intro.en: Friendly shows the English suffix -ly at work twice: once as an adjective ending and once, in the adverb, as a manner ending.
intro.cn: friendly 展示了英语后缀 -ly 的两种工作方式：一次作形容词词尾，一次在副词中作方式词尾。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, not Latin: friend plus the Old English suffix -lic, which became -ly.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语而非拉丁语：friend 加古英语后缀 -lic，后者演变为 -ly。

items.example: The noun supplies the model the adjective imitates.
items.exampleCN: 名词提供了形容词所模仿的原型。

items.example: The suffix turns a person into a manner.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把人变成一种举止方式。

items.example: The old woman was friendly from the first morning.
items.exampleCN: 那位老人从第一个早晨就很亲切。

items.example: Friendliness costs nothing and opens most doors.
items.exampleCN: 友善不花钱，却能打开大多数门。

items.example: The clerk was efficient but unfriendly.
items.exampleCN: 那名职员效率很高，却不友善。

items.structure: user + friendly (compounded in the twentieth century)
items.example: The old software was powerful but never user-friendly.
items.exampleCN: 旧软件功能强大，却从不便于使用。

items.example: They chose an environment-friendly detergent.
items.exampleCN: 他们选了环保洗涤剂。

items.meaning: to act as a friend toward
items.example: She befriended the new pupil on his first day.
items.exampleCN: 新同学第一天她就与他结为朋友。

definition_zh: 把……联系起来；与人交往；使加入；同事；伙伴；（职称）副的；准会员
definition_en: to connect one thing with another, or a person connected with a group or a business
core_image: 两张桌子被推到同一面墙下，桌上的两摞文件彼此倚着，谁也没有单独挪走
scene: 散会后，两个人把自己的椅子搬到同一张桌旁，文件摊开，各自写下的名字旁都划了同一条线。The two researchers pushed their chairs to one table, and by the end of the afternoon their names were being used as one associate of the other.
sceneCN: 这里 associate 指「把人或事物联系在一起、结成伙伴」（第 1 个义项：在头脑或事实上把两者联结起来）；句意为两位研究者把椅子搬到同一张桌旁，到下午他们的名字已被当作彼此的合作者。可辨识物件：同一张桌、两摞文件、并排的椅子、划线的笔。

pos.zh: 把……联系起来；使联合；使加入
交往；结交（常与 with 连用）
同事；伙伴；准会员；联营机构
副的；准的；联合的

senses.title: Link one thing with another in the mind
senses.titleCN: 在头脑中把两者联系起来
senses.definition: to connect an idea, a name or an object with something else
senses.definitionCN: 把某个想法、名字或物件与另一事物相连
senses.example: Most readers associate that smell with their first school.
senses.exampleCN: 多数读者会把那种气味与自己第一所学校联系起来。
senses.why: Ad- 'to' plus socius 'companion' gave the Latin verb 'to join with'; joining two things in thought is the first step of that joining.
senses.whyCN: ad-「朝向」加 socius「同伴」构成拉丁动词「与……联合」；在思想中把两件事并在一起，正是这种联合的第一步。

senses.title: Spend time with certain people
senses.definition: to spend time with people or groups, often with a hint of disapproval
senses.definitionCN: 与某些人或群体来往，常带轻微的贬义
senses.example: He associated with gamblers for two years and lost his savings.
senses.exampleCN: 他与赌徒厮混了两年，把积蓄赔了进去。
senses.why: Joining a group by choice is the social form of the same verb, and the tone turns negative when the group is disreputable.
senses.whyCN: 自愿加入某个群体，是同一动词的社会形式；当这群人名声不佳时，语气就转为负面。

senses.title: Join a firm or enterprise
senses.definition: to join another person or firm as a partner in an enterprise
senses.definitionCN: 作为合作者加入另一人或另一家企业的经营
senses.example: She associated herself with a small printing house.
senses.exampleCN: 她与一家小型印刷所合伙经营。
senses.why: The commercial sense is the joining of equals in a venture, which is why the noun later names such a partner.
senses.whyCN: 商业义指平等者在事业中联合，因此名词后来就用以指这样的合作者。

senses.title: A colleague in work or business
senses.definition: a person who works with you, especially in business or a profession
senses.definitionCN: 与你共事的人，尤指生意或专业领域中的伙伴
senses.example: A business associate called about the contract at midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 一位生意伙伴半夜打电话来谈合同。
senses.why: One who has been joined to you in a venture is naturally called by the same word as the act of joining.
senses.whyCN: 在事业上与你联合的人，自然就用表示联合的那个词来称呼。

senses.title: A member of lower standing in a body
senses.definition: a member of a professional body who has not yet reached full fellowship
senses.definitionCN: 专业团体中尚未达到正式会士资格的成员
senses.example: She was an associate of the college for six years before becoming a fellow.
senses.exampleCN: 她做了六年准会员，之后才转为正式会士。
senses.why: Professional bodies rank their members, and the entry grade is named for being joined to the body without full rights.
senses.whyCN: 专业团体对会员分等级，入门等级之名源于「已加入团体但权利未满」。

senses.title: A secondary rank in a title
senses.definition: of a rank just below the senior one, as in associate professor
senses.definitionCN: 级别略低于正职的，如副教授
senses.example: He was promoted to associate professor last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 去年春天他升为副教授。
senses.why: A rank that stands beside the full rank, not equal to it, takes the adjective from the same family.
senses.whyCN: 与正职并列却不相等的职级，用了同一词族的形容词形式。

senses.title: A thing linked by a relation
senses.definition: a thing that accompanies or is connected with another, often in a set phrase
senses.definitionCN: 与另一事物相伴或相连的东西，常用于固定说法
senses.example: The bone is a strange associate of the old fever.
senses.exampleCN: 这块骨头是那种古老热病一个奇怪的伴生物。
senses.why: Once the verb can join any two things, the noun can name anything joined, not only people.
senses.whyCN: 动词一旦能连接任意两物，名词也就能指任何被连接之物，而不限于人。

senses.title: A file type tied to an application
senses.titleCN: 文件类型与程序的关联
senses.definition: to link a file type with the program that opens it
senses.definitionCN: 把某种文件类型与打开它的程序绑定
senses.example: The installer associated the image files with the new viewer.
senses.exampleCN: 安装程序把图像文件与新看图软件关联起来。
senses.why: Computers reuse the oldest sense literally: two things that were separate are made to open together.
senses.whyCN: 计算机字面地沿用最古老的义项：两件本来分开的东西被设成一起打开。

intro.en: Associate comes from Latin associare 'to join with', built on ad- 'to' and socius 'companion, ally'. The noun socius is generally thought to be related to sequi 'to follow'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: associate 来自拉丁 associare「与……联合」，由 ad-「朝向」与 socius「同伴、盟友」构成。名词 socius 一般被认为与 sequi「跟随」有关。下列年代均为约数。

items.en: Socius named a companion, an ally or a partner in trade. Its link to sequi 'to follow' is generally accepted but not beyond argument, and the deeper Indo-European form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: socius 指同伴、盟友或生意上的合伙人。它与 sequi「跟随」的联系被普遍接受，但并非毫无争议，更深的印欧形式属重构。

items.en: The prefix ad- 'to, toward' assimilates to the following consonant; it marks direction and the beginning of a union.
items.cn: 前缀 ad-「朝向」会随后面的辅音同化；它标示方向，也标示一段联合的开端。

items.en: Ad- plus socius produced associare, 'to join to oneself as a companion, to unite'. The verb is recorded in classical texts.
items.cn: ad- 加 socius 构成 associare，意为「把……收作同伴、使联合」。该动词在古典文献中有书证。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the sixteenth century and the noun associate soon after, first in the sense of a partner in office or business.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个动词，不久后有了名词 associate，最初指职务或生意上的伙伴。

items.en: Source uncertain (first English date and deeper root): the earliest English citation is not fixed with confidence, and the connection of socius to the verb for following rests on inference, with its Indo-European ancestor only a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（英语首见年代与更深词根）：最早的英语书证无法确定；socius 与表示「跟随」的动词之间的联系属于推断，其印欧祖形只是重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root nouns and verbs that are constantly mixed up with associate, plus one prefixed opposite; group two holds the people and verbs that mean roughly the same.
note.cn: 第一组是同根且最易与 associate 混淆的名词与动词，另加一个加前缀的反义词；第二组是意义大致相同的人与动词。

entries.definition: Built on socius with the ending -alis: it describes life in groups, not the act of joining one person to another.
entries.definitionCN: 由 socius 加 -alis 构成：它描述群体生活，而非把某人与另一人联结的动作。

entries.definition: The whole body of people living together; associate names a link between individuals, society names the aggregate.
entries.definitionCN: 共同生活的人群整体；associate 指个体间的联结，society 指这个整体。

entries.definition: Ready to mix with others; it describes a disposition, while associate describes an actual connection.
entries.definitionCN: 乐于与人交往；它描述性情，而 associate 描述实际存在的联结。

entries.definition: Dis- 'apart' plus the same verb: to separate in the mind or in fact, the exact reverse of associating.
entries.definitionCN: dis-「分开」加同一动词：在思想上或事实上分离，正是 associate 的反面。

entries.definition: A person you work with in the same organization; it is neutral and does not imply ownership or partnership.
entries.definitionCN: 同一组织中共事的人；语气中性，不含合伙或共同所有权之意。

entries.definition: Someone who shares a business, a task or a life with a defined share; it is stronger than associate in commitment.
entries.definitionCN: 在生意、任务或生活中按确定份额共担的人；在投入程度上比 associate 更强。

entries.definition: To attach an organization to a larger one; the link is structural, while associate usually implies people or ideas.
entries.definitionCN: 把一个机构附属于更大的机构；这种联结是结构性的，而 associate 通常指人或观念。

entries.definition: The everyday verb for joining two things; associate is its mental and professional counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 连接两物的日常动词；associate 是它在思维与职业领域的对应词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin companion word, the real prefix and the real title phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁「同伴」词、真实的前缀，以及真实的职称搭配。

normal.en: Ad- 'to' plus socius 'companion': to join a companion to yourself.
normal.cn: ad-「朝向」加 socius「同伴」：把一个同伴并到自己身边。

normal.en: The same root gives social, society and sociable, all about being together.
normal.cn: 同一词根衍生 social、society 与 sociable，都与「待在一起」有关。

normal.en: Titles mark the junior rank: associate professor, associate director, associate member.
normal.cn: 职称标出较低职级：副教授、副总监、准会员。

normal.en: Dissociate is the exact reverse, built by swapping the prefix.
normal.cn: dissociate 正是其反面，靠换前缀构成。

normal.en: In computing the verb is used literally: a file type is associated with the program that opens it.
normal.cn: 在计算机里这个动词被字面使用：某种文件类型与打开它的程序建立关联。

abstract.en: Picture two chairs pushed to the same table until the arms touch.
abstract.cn: 想象两把椅子被推到同一张桌旁，扶手相碰。

abstract.en: Picture a name written on a form beside another name, linked by a single line.
abstract.cn: 想象表格上一个名字写在另一个名字旁，中间只画了一条线。

abstract.en: Picture an idea that always brings a particular smell with it, uninvited.
abstract.cn: 想象一个念头总是不请自来地带起某种气味。

examples.en: Patients often associate a hospital smell with bad news.
examples.cn: 病人常把医院的气味与坏消息联系起来。

examples.en: She became an associate of the firm after eight years as a clerk.
examples.cn: 做了八年职员之后，她成了这家事务所的合伙人。

examples.en: Do not associate with people who borrow money and forget it.
examples.cn: 不要与借钱就忘的人来往。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「a（一个）+ soci（同伴）」——把一个人并到同伴那一群里 → 联系、交往、同事

root: 拉丁 associare「使联合」= ad-（朝向）+ socius（同伴、盟友）；socius 与「跟随」的联系属推断，更深印欧祖形为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act: putting two things at the same table. It begins with ideas linked in the mind, moves to people chosen as company, then to a firm joined, the colleague who results, the junior grade in a professional body, a secondary title, any connected thing, and finally a file type bound to a program.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一个动作展开：把两样东西放到同一张桌旁。它先指脑中相连的观念，再指被选作同伴的人、加入的事务所、由此而来的同事、专业团体中的低阶会员、副职头衔、任何相连之物，最后是绑定到某个程序的文件类型。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two chairs pulled up to one table until the arms touch.
core.cn: 核心意象：两把椅子被拉到同一张桌旁，扶手相碰。

branches.en: JOINING IN THOUGHT AND FACT: an idea carries another idea with it, and any two things can be named as joined.
branches.cn: 思想上与事实上的联结：一个观念带出另一个观念，任何两件东西也都能被说成相连。

branches.en: CHOSEN COMPANY: the social form of the same verb, with a tone that turns when the company is dubious.
branches.cn: 自选的同伴：同一动词的社会形式，当同伴名声不佳时语气也随之转冷。

branches.en: FIRM AND COLLEAGUE: the venture joined, and the person who is thereby joined to you.
branches.cn: 事务所与同事：加入的事业，以及因此与你联合的那个人。

branches.en: STANDING BESIDE, NOT EQUAL: the junior grade in a professional body and the secondary rank in a title.
branches.cn: 并列而不对等：专业团体中的低阶会员，以及头衔里的副职。

branches.en: THE MACHINE VERSION: two separate things made to open together by a setting.
branches.cn: 机器版本：两件分开的东西被一项设置成一起打开。

intro.en: Associate splits into a Latin prefix and a Latin companion word, both of which still appear across English.
intro.cn: associate 可拆为一个拉丁前缀与一个拉丁「同伴」词，两者至今仍出现在大量英语词中。

latinIntro.en: Latin socius builds social, society, sociable and associate; ad- adds direction and the start of a union.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 socius 构成 social、society、sociable 与 associate；ad- 增添方向与联合的开端。

items.example: The prefix marks the direction of the joining.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出联合的方向。

items.example: The root supplies the person who is joined.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供被联合的那个人。

items.example: The verb named the act before English named the person.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词先命名动作，英语后来才命名人。

items.example: Most readers associate that smell with school.
items.exampleCN: 多数读者把那种气味与学校联系起来。

items.meaning: the act or body formed by joining
items.example: The association meets twice a year.
items.exampleCN: 该协会每年开两次会。

items.example: Associative memory links smells to places.
items.exampleCN: 联想记忆把气味与地点连在一起。

items.example: Only associable ideas survive in a list.
items.exampleCN: 只有能相互联结的观念才能在清单里留存。

items.example: He dissociated himself from the decision.
items.exampleCN: 他与那项决定撇清了关系。

items.example: Social life changed after the mill closed.
items.exampleCN: 工厂关闭后，群体生活发生了变化。

definition_zh: 隶属关系；所属机构；加入；渊源；教派归属
definition_en: the state of being officially attached to an organization, or the body so attached
core_image: 一张表格的页脚处，写着一个机构的名字，笔迹压得很重，好像要把人钉在那里
scene: 报名表的最后一栏要求填写所属单位，投稿人把研究所的名字写了两遍，怕别人看不清。On the last line of the form the author wrote his affiliation twice, in case the committee could not read it.
sceneCN: 这里 affiliation 指「一个人正式所属的机构或团体」（第 2 个义项：表格上所列的所属单位）；句意为作者在表格末行把所属研究所写了两遍，怕评审看不清。可辨识物件：表格、末行、重复的名字、钢笔。

pos.zh: 隶属关系；所属机构；加入；渊源；教派归属

derivatives.zh: 倾向于建立联结的（心理学用语）

senses.title: Being formally attached to a body
senses.titleCN: 正式隶属于某机构的状态
senses.definition: the state of being officially connected with an organization
senses.definitionCN: 与某个组织存在正式联系的状态
senses.example: Her affiliation with the laboratory began during her doctoral years.
senses.exampleCN: 她与这家实验室的隶属关系始于读博期间。
senses.why: The medieval Latin verb first meant to adopt as a son; a body that takes a person in repeats that gesture in institutional form.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪拉丁动词原指「收为养子」；一个机构把人纳入，正是以制度形式重演这一动作。

senses.title: The body named on the form
senses.titleCN: 表格上填写的所属单位
senses.definition: the organization that a person lists as their home institution
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在正式场合登记的所属机构
senses.example: Please give your name, post and affiliation at the top of the page.
senses.exampleCN: 请在页面顶端写明姓名、职务与所属单位。
senses.why: Conferences and journals need to know where a person stands, so the abstract state turned into a slot on a form.
senses.whyCN: 会议与期刊需要知道一个人站在哪里，于是这一抽象状态变成了表格上的一栏。

senses.title: The act of joining or adopting
senses.definition: the act of attaching a person or group to a larger body
senses.definitionCN: 把人或团体纳入更大机构的行为
senses.example: The affiliation of the smaller colleges took three years to complete.
senses.exampleCN: 这些小学院的并入花了三年才完成。
senses.why: The noun covers the act as well as the result, because a joining is both something done and something that then exists.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词既指行为也指结果，因为一次并入既是被做成的事，也是随之存在的状态。

senses.title: A local branch of a larger body
senses.titleCN: 隶属于大机构的本地分支
senses.definition: a local group or branch attached to a national or parent organization
senses.definitionCN: 附属于全国性或母机构的本地团体或分支
senses.example: The county association is an affiliation of the national union.
senses.exampleCN: 县协会是全国工会的一个下属分支。
senses.why: Once a body can be adopted, it can also adopt others, and the word names the junior body as well as the link.
senses.whyCN: 一个机构既能被收编，也能收编别人，于是这个词既指联结，也指较低一级的机构本身。

senses.title: The line a thing comes from
senses.definition: the origin or source of a work, idea or practice
senses.definitionCN: 作品、思想或做法的来源
senses.example: The manuscript's affiliation with the northern school is still disputed.
senses.exampleCN: 这份手稿与北方学派的渊源仍有争议。
senses.why: People are attached to institutions; works are attached to traditions, and the same word carries the second attachment.
senses.whyCN: 人被归属于机构，作品被归属于传统，同一个词承担了这第二种归属。

senses.title: The need to belong to a group
senses.titleCN: 归属于群体的心理需要
senses.definition: in psychology, the basic motive to form and keep social connections
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中指形成并维持社会联系的基本动机
senses.example: The study measured affiliation needs in first-year students.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究测量了一年级学生的归属需要。
senses.why: Social psychology turned the institutional noun inward, naming a drive rather than a membership card.
senses.whyCN: 社会心理学把这个制度性名词转向内心，命名的是一种驱力，而不是一张会员证。

senses.title: A link through family or marriage
senses.titleCN: 因血缘或婚姻而来的关联
senses.definition: a connection established through kinship or marriage
senses.definitionCN: 通过亲属或婚姻建立的联系
senses.example: His affiliation to the founding family is through his grandmother.
senses.exampleCN: 他与创建者家族的关联来自他的祖母。
senses.why: Adoption was the original sense, so kinship is the oldest layer the word still carries.
senses.whyCN: 「收养」是这个词最初的意思，因此血缘是它至今保留的最古老的一层。

senses.title: Membership in a religious body
senses.definition: formal membership in a church or denomination
senses.definitionCN: 在某一教会或教派中的正式成员身份
senses.example: The survey asked about affiliation rather than attendance.
senses.exampleCN: 调查问的是宗教归属，而不是出席频率。
senses.why: Surveys separate what a person is attached to from what a person does, which is exactly the line this word draws.
senses.whyCN: 调查把一个人「挂在哪个名下」与「实际做什么」分开，而这正是这个词划出的界线。

intro.en: Affiliation comes from Medieval Latin affiliatio, from the verb affiliare 'to adopt as a son', built on ad- 'to' and filius 'son'. The institutional sense is later. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: affiliation 来自中世纪拉丁 affiliatio，其动词 affiliare 意为「收为养子」，由 ad-「朝向」与 filius「儿子」构成。制度义出现较晚。下列年代均为约数。

items.en: Filius 'son' is well recorded. Its deeper origin is generally thought to involve a root connected with suckling, but that account is a reconstruction and not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: filius「儿子」有充分书证。其更深来源一般被认为与表示「吮吸」的词根有关，但这一说法属重构，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Ad- 'to, toward' assimilates before f and marks the direction of the attachment.
items.cn: ad-「朝向」在 f 前发生同化，标示这种归属关系的方向。

items.en: Affiliare meant 'to adopt as a son, to receive into a family'. The verb belongs to medieval legal and ecclesiastical Latin; its first appearance cannot be dated precisely.
items.cn: affiliare 意为「收为养子、纳入家族」。该动词属中世纪法律与教会拉丁语，其首见年代无法定出。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the word was used for bodies attached to larger bodies, and adoption faded into the background.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，这个词用于附属于更大机构的团体，收养义退到背景中。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper root): the medieval first citation is not fixed, the root of filius is a reconstruction rather than a proven form, and the exact route from adoption to institutional attachment is inferred from usage.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词根）：中世纪的最早书证无法确定；filius 的词根属重构而非已证形式；从收养义到机构归属义的确切路径是从用法中推断的。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root words and one near look-alike with a completely different root; group two holds the words for belonging to something.
note.cn: 第一组是同根词，外加一个字形相近却词根完全不同的词；第二组是表示「归属于某处」的词。

entries.definition: The verb and the branch noun built on the same adoption root; affiliation is the state or the link, not the body or the act itself.
entries.definitionCN: 由同一「收养」词根构成的动词与分支名词；affiliation 指状态或联结，而非机构或行为本身。

entries.definition: The adjective for having such a link, as in an affiliated college; it describes the member, while affiliation names the relationship.
entries.definitionCN: 表示拥有这种联结的形容词，如附属学院；它描述成员，而 affiliation 命名关系。

entries.definition: Built directly on filius 'son': it means of a son or daughter, as in filial duty, and has nothing institutional about it.
entries.definitionCN: 直接由 filius「儿子」构成：意为子女的，如孝道，与机构毫无关系。

entries.definition: Ad- plus finis 'border': a natural attraction or likeness, with no adoption and no membership in its root.
entries.definitionCN: ad- 加 finis「边界」：天生的吸引或相似，词根里既没有收养，也没有会员。

entries.definition: The state of being a member, often with rights and dues; affiliation is looser and can be only a listed address.
entries.definitionCN: 成员身份，常含权利与会费；affiliation 更松散，有时只是登记的一个所属单位。

entries.definition: An organized body of people, or the act of joining one; affiliation usually names the link to a body already formed.
entries.definitionCN: 有组织的人群团体，或加入团体的行为；affiliation 通常指与已存在的机构之间的联结。

entries.definition: Duty of loyalty to a sovereign or cause; it is moral and binding, while affiliation can be a line on a form.
entries.definitionCN: 对君主或事业应尽的忠诚；它是道德且具约束力的，而 affiliation 可能只是表格上的一行。

entries.definition: Any link or fastening, physical or emotional; affiliation is the institutional species of attachment.
entries.definitionCN: 任何联结或固定，无论实体还是情感；affiliation 是这种联结在制度层面的种类。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin son word, the real institutional phrases and the real derived forms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁「儿子」词、真实的机构搭配，以及真实的派生形式。

normal.en: Ad- plus filius 'son': the original act was taking someone into a family, and a body taking you in repeats it.
normal.cn: ad- 加 filius「儿子」：最初的动作是把人纳入一个家庭，而机构把你纳入，正是重演这一动作。

normal.en: The same son root appears in filial, which keeps the family sense untouched by institutions.
normal.cn: 同一个「儿子」词根也出现在 filial 中，那里仍是纯粹的家庭义，与机构无关。

normal.en: Forms ask for it explicitly: name, post and affiliation, institutional affiliation.
normal.cn: 各类表格会明确要求：姓名、职务与所属单位、机构隶属。

normal.en: Political, religious and party affiliation are the common fixed phrases.
normal.cn: 政治归属、宗教归属与党派归属是最常见的固定搭配。

normal.en: The verb behind it is affiliate, and the negative is unaffiliated, meaning attached to nothing.
normal.cn: 它背后的动词是 affiliate，其否定式 unaffiliated 意为不隶属任何机构。

abstract.en: Picture a name written at the foot of a page, pressed hard enough to emboss the paper.
abstract.cn: 想象一个名字写在页脚，笔力重到把纸压出凹痕。

abstract.en: Picture a small branch office whose sign carries the parent name in smaller letters.
abstract.cn: 想象一间小分支机构的招牌，母机构的名字用更小的字写在下面。

abstract.en: Picture a child holding an adult's hand in a crowd, not because of blood but because someone took the hand.
abstract.cn: 想象人群中一个孩子牵着大人的手，不是因为血缘，而是因为有人先伸出了手。

examples.en: The journal requires authors to state their institutional affiliation.
examples.cn: 该期刊要求作者写明所属机构。

examples.en: Her political affiliation changed twice during the campaign.
examples.cn: 竞选期间她的政治归属变了两次。

examples.en: The survey records religious affiliation separately from practice.
examples.cn: 该调查把宗教归属与实际宗教活动分开记录。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「a（朝向）+ fili（儿子）」——被收作儿子、纳入家门 → 隶属、所属机构

root: 中世纪拉丁 affiliatio「收为养子」= ad-（朝向）+ filius（儿子）；制度上的「隶属」义由此引申；filius 更深词根属重构，不作定论。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one adoption: a body takes a person in, the person writes that body on a form, the act of taking in, the branch that results, the line a work comes from, the inward need to belong, the kinship link, and finally the denomination a survey asks about.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一次收纳入门展开：机构把人纳入、人在表格上写下这个机构、纳入这一行为本身、由此产生的分支、作品所属的源流、内心对归属的需要、血缘上的关联，最后是调查所问的教派归属。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a name written at the foot of a page, pressed hard into the paper.
core.cn: 核心意象：写在页脚的一个名字，笔力把纸压出痕迹。

branches.en: THE LINK AND ITS LABEL: being attached to a body, and the body that gets written down as yours.
branches.cn: 联结与标签：隶属于某机构，以及被写成你所属的那个机构。

branches.en: ACT AND RESULT: the joining performed, and the junior body that exists once it is done.
branches.cn: 行为与结果：被执行的并入，以及并入之后存在的下级机构。

branches.en: WORKS ATTACHED TOO: a manuscript can belong to a school the way a person belongs to an institute.
branches.cn: 作品也有归属：手稿属于某一学派，正如人属于某一研究所。

branches.en: THE INWARD TURN: psychology renames the membership card as a motive to belong.
branches.cn: 由外转内：心理学把会员证改写成一种归属动机。

branches.en: KIN AND CREED: the oldest adoption layer in family links, and the modern form's question about religion.
branches.cn: 血缘与信仰：家庭关联中那层最古老的「收养」义，以及现代表格对宗教的询问。

intro.en: Affiliation is a Latin verb noun built on the word for a son, so its family shows the whole path from family to institution.
intro.cn: affiliation 是由拉丁动词派生的名词，其词根是表示「儿子」的词，因此这一词族完整展示了从家庭到机构的路径。

latinIntro.en: Latin filius yields affiliation, affiliate, filial and filiation; ad- adds direction, and -atio marks the action or its result.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 filius 衍生 affiliation、affiliate、filial 与 filiation；ad- 增添方向，-atio 标示动作或结果。

items.example: The prefix points the attachment toward a body.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把归属指向某个机构。

items.example: The root supplies the family image at the base of the word.
items.exampleCN: 词根提供这个词底层的家庭意象。

items.example: The medieval verb named adoption before it named membership.
items.exampleCN: 这个中世纪动词先指收养，后指会员身份。

items.meaning: the state or act of being attached
items.example: Her affiliation with the laboratory began in her doctoral years.
items.exampleCN: 她与实验室的隶属关系始于读博期间。

items.example: The clinic is an affiliate of the teaching hospital.
items.exampleCN: 这家诊所是教学医院的附属机构。

items.example: Three affiliated colleges share the library.
items.exampleCN: 三所附属学院共用这座图书馆。

items.example: Unaffiliated researchers may still use the archive.
items.exampleCN: 无所属机构的研究者仍可使用该档案。

items.example: Filial duty kept him in the old house.
items.exampleCN: 子女的责任让他留在老宅里。

items.meaning: the relation of child to parent
items.example: The monastery traced its filiation to an older house.
items.exampleCN: 这座修道院把自己的源流追溯到更早的院所。

latinEntries.structure: affiliatio, affiliationis (f., third declension, Medieval Latin)

definition_zh: 使隶属；加入；分支机构；联营公司；（作定语）附属的
definition_en: to attach an organization to a larger one, or a body so attached
core_image: 一棵小树把根接到老树的根系上，地面上的两段树干却各自站着
scene: 学院挂牌那天，院长在旧木牌旁钉上一块新牌，新牌上的院名比母大学的名字小一号。On the day the college opened, the dean fixed a new sign beside the old one, with the college name set one size smaller than the university it had joined as an affiliate.
sceneCN: 这里 affiliate 作名词，指「附属于更大机构的单位」（第 3 个义项：附属机构、分支机构）；句意为学院挂牌时，新牌上的院名比它所附属的大学小一号。可辨识物件：两块木牌、锤子、大小不同的字体、门口的台阶。

pos.zh: 使隶属；使加入；追溯……的来源
加入；结盟（与 with 连用）
分支机构；附属机构；联营公司；成员组织
附属的；有关联的

senses.title: Attach a body to a larger one
senses.titleCN: 把一个机构接到更大机构之下
senses.definition: to bring an organization into formal connection with a larger one
senses.definitionCN: 使某组织与更大机构建立正式联系
senses.example: The university affiliated the small conservatory in 1958.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学于 1958 年把这家小型音乐学院纳入旗下。
senses.why: The medieval verb meant to adopt as a son; an institution taking another under its name performs the same act on paper.
senses.whyCN: 这个中世纪动词意为「收为养子」；一个机构把另一个收归名下，就是在纸面上重演同一动作。

senses.title: Join a group oneself
senses.definition: to join or connect oneself with a group or movement
senses.definitionCN: 自行加入某团体或运动并与之建立联系
senses.example: The clinic affiliated with a teaching hospital to share staff.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所与一家教学医院建立联系，以共享人员。
senses.why: The same verb works in both directions: a parent can affiliate a child body, and a body can affiliate itself.
senses.whyCN: 同一动词两个方向都成立：母机构可以收编下属，下属机构也可以自行投靠。

senses.title: A branch under a parent body
senses.definition: an organization attached to and partly controlled by a larger one
senses.definitionCN: 附属于较大机构并受其部分管理组织
senses.example: Each affiliate keeps its own budget and its own trustees.
senses.exampleCN: 每个附属机构都有自己的预算与理事会。
senses.why: Once the act is done, the body that results needs a name, and the same word serves as a noun.
senses.whyCN: 动作一旦完成，由此产生的机构就需要一个名字，于是同一个词又作名词。

senses.title: A partner that sells for another
senses.titleCN: 代销他人产品的联营方
senses.definition: a company or website that promotes another company's products for a share of the sales
senses.definitionCN: 为另一家公司推广产品并按销售额分成的公司或网站
senses.example: The software firm pays its affiliates a share of each sale.
senses.exampleCN: 这家软件公司把每笔销售额的一部分付给推广伙伴。
senses.why: Modern commerce revived the noun for a body that carries another's name without being owned by it.
senses.whyCN: 现代商业让这个名词复活，指打着别人旗号却并不被其拥有的机构。

senses.title: Carrying attached status
senses.definition: having a secondary or attached status, used before another noun
senses.definitionCN: 具有次级或附属身份，用于另一名词之前
senses.example: She serves as an affiliate member of the ethics board.
senses.exampleCN: 她担任伦理委员会的附属会员。
senses.why: The adjectival use simply compresses the whole relationship into a label that can sit before a title.
senses.whyCN: 形容词用法把整段关系压缩成一个可以放在头衔前的标签。

senses.title: Trace a line of origin
senses.definition: to trace the origin of a body or a practice to an earlier source
senses.definitionCN: 把某机构或做法的来源追溯到更早的源头
senses.example: The order affiliates its rule to a monastery in the south.
senses.exampleCN: 该修会把自己的会规追溯到南方的一座修道院。
senses.why: Adoption was the original sense, so tracing who came from whom survived as a learned use of the verb.
senses.whyCN: 「收养」是最初的意思，因此追溯谁出自谁这一用法作为书面义保留了下来。

senses.title: A person loosely connected
senses.titleCN: 与机构关系松散的个人
senses.definition: a person connected with an institution without full membership
senses.definitionCN: 与某机构有联系但无完整成员身份的人
senses.example: Several affiliates teach one course each and hold no vote.
senses.exampleCN: 几位附属人员各教一门课，没有投票权。
senses.why: Institutions need a name for people who work with them without belonging fully, and the noun stretches to cover them.
senses.whyCN: 机构需要一个词来称呼为其工作却并未完全归属的人，名词因此延伸到这类人身上。

senses.title: A local station under a network
senses.definition: a local radio or television station that carries a national network's programming
senses.definitionCN: 播放全国性联播网节目的地方广播或电视台
senses.example: The local affiliate added two hours of its own reporting.
senses.exampleCN: 这家地方附属台增加了两小时自采报道。
senses.why: Broadcasting borrowed the word because a local station carries a national name without being owned by it.
senses.whyCN: 广播业借用这个词，因为地方台打着全国性的名字，却并不归其所有。

intro.en: Affiliate comes from Medieval Latin affiliare 'to adopt as a son', built on ad- 'to' and filius 'son'. English borrowed the verb in the sixteenth century and made the noun from it. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: affiliate 来自中世纪拉丁 affiliare「收为养子」，由 ad-「朝向」与 filius「儿子」构成。英语在十六世纪借入这个动词，并由它造出名词。下列年代均为约数。

items.en: Filius 'son' is securely recorded. The deeper origin is generally thought to involve a root connected with suckling, but that is a reconstruction rather than a proven derivation.
items.cn: filius「儿子」书证确凿。更深来源一般被认为与表示「吮吸」的词根有关，但那属重构，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: The verb affiliare meant 'to adopt as a son, to receive into a family'. It belongs to medieval legal and church Latin, and its first appearance is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 动词 affiliare 意为「收为养子、纳入家族」。它属中世纪法律与教会拉丁语，首见年代无确切记录。

items.en: English took the verb in the sixteenth century for joining a person or body to another; the earliest citation is not firmly fixed.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入该动词，用于把人或机构与另一机构联结；最早书证并无确证。

items.en: The noun affiliate appeared later for the junior body itself, and modern commerce and broadcasting added the partner and local-station senses.
items.cn: 名词 affiliate 后来才出现，指较低一级的机构本身；现代商业与广播业又增添了联营方与地方台的义项。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates and deeper root): neither the medieval nor the English first citation is fixed with confidence, and the root of filius is a reconstruction, so the family image at the base is inferred rather than proven.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词根）：中世纪与英语的最早书证都无确证；filius 的词根属重构，因此词底的家庭意象属推断而非已证。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root nouns and adjectives plus one near look-alike with an unrelated root; group two holds the bodies and words that describe a subordinate organization.
note.cn: 第一组是同根名词与形容词，另加一个字形相近却不同源的词；第二组是描述下属机构的名词与词。

entries.definition: The state or link itself; affiliate names the body or the act, while affiliation names what that body has with its parent.
entries.definitionCN: 指状态或联结本身；affiliate 指机构或行为，而 affiliation 指该机构与母体之间所拥有的关系。

entries.definition: The participle used as an adjective for bodies that are attached; the noun affiliate can be the body, the adjective describes it.
entries.definitionCN: 用来说明已附属于某方的机构的分词形容词；名词 affiliate 可以是那个机构，形容词则描述它。

entries.definition: Of a son or daughter, built straight on filius; it keeps the family sense and never means institutional attachment.
entries.definitionCN: 子女的，直接由 filius 构成；它保留家庭义，从不表示机构归属。

entries.definition: Ad- plus finis 'border': a natural likeness or attraction, with no son and no adoption in its root.
entries.definitionCN: ad- 加 finis「边界」：天生的相似或吸引，词根里既无「儿子」也无「收养」。

entries.definition: A company controlled by a parent that owns most of its shares; affiliate implies a looser link without ownership.
entries.definitionCN: 由持股多数的母公司控制的公司；affiliate 所指的是更松、且不含所有权的联结。

entries.definition: A local office of the same organization; an affiliate is a separate body carrying the name, not the same firm's office.
entries.definitionCN: 同一组织的本地办事处；affiliate 是打着名号的独立机构，而非同一公司的办事处。

entries.definition: A party sharing a business on agreed terms; affiliation stresses a hierarchy that partnership does not.
entries.definitionCN: 按约定条件共担生意的一方；affiliation 强调层级，而合伙关系不含这种层级。

entries.definition: A colleague or linked firm without formal attachment; affiliate usually implies a documented link to a parent body.
entries.definitionCN: 有关联的同事或公司，但无正式归属；affiliate 通常含与母机构之间有据可查的联结。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real son root, the real business phrases and the real derived words of the verb.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「儿子」词根、真实的商业搭配，以及这个动词真实的派生词。

normal.en: Ad- plus filius 'son': adopting a body under a name is the institutional version of taking in a child.
normal.cn: ad- 加 filius「儿子」：把一个机构收归名下，是「把孩子接进家门」的制度版本。

normal.en: Filial keeps the family sense of the same root, so the two words can be told apart by their settings.
normal.cn: filial 保留了同一词根的家庭义，因此两个词可以靠使用场合区分。

normal.en: Business phrases: affiliate program, affiliate network, affiliated company.
normal.cn: 商业搭配：联盟推广计划、联盟网络、联营公司。

normal.en: The pair affiliation and affiliate divides neatly into state and body.
normal.cn: affiliation 与 affiliate 这对词恰好分成「状态」与「机构」。

normal.en: Broadcasting uses it for a local station that carries a national name without being owned.
normal.cn: 广播业用它指打着全国名号却并不被其所有的地方台。

abstract.en: Picture a young tree whose roots have grafted onto an older root system, while both trunks still stand apart.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵小树的根接到了老树的根系上，两段树干却各自立着。

abstract.en: Picture a new sign bolted beside an old one, the smaller name deliberately set lower.
abstract.cn: 想象一块新牌钉在旧牌旁，较小的名字被特意放低。

abstract.en: Picture a shop that flies another company's flag but keeps its own till.
abstract.cn: 想象一家店挂着他公司的旗，却用自己的收银机。

examples.en: The research centre is an affiliate of the medical school.
examples.cn: 这个研究中心是医学院的附属机构。

examples.en: Small publishers can affiliate with a larger distributor to reach bookshops.
examples.cn: 小出版社可以与较大的发行商结盟，从而进入书店。

examples.en: The station became an affiliate of the national network in the 1970s.
examples.cn: 这家电台在二十世纪七十年代成为全国联播网的附属台。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「a（朝向）+ fili（儿子）」——把机构收作「儿子」挂在名下 → 使隶属、附属机构

root: 中世纪拉丁 affiliare「收为养子」= ad-（朝向）+ filius（儿子）；由「纳入家族」引申为「使机构隶属」。filius 更深词根属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one grafting: a body is adopted under a name, a body adopts itself, the branch that results, the partner that carries the name without being owned, the label of attached status, the tracing of origin, the loosely attached person, and the local station under a national flag.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一次「接根」展开：机构被收归名下、机构自行投靠、由此产生的分支、打着名号却不被拥有的联营方、附属身份的标签、对源流的追溯、关系松散的个人，以及挂着全国旗号的地方台。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a young trunk grafted onto an older root system while both trunks still stand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一棵小树嫁接到老树的根系上，两段树干却各自立着。

branches.en: THE ACT OF TAKING IN: attaching a body under a name, and the learned tracing of who came from whom.
branches.cn: 纳入的动作：把机构收归名下，以及书面上追溯谁出自谁。

branches.en: SELF-ATTACHMENT: a body that joins a larger one of its own accord.
branches.cn: 自行投靠：机构主动加入更大的机构。

branches.en: WHAT RESULTS: the branch that exists afterwards, and the person who works with it without full membership.
branches.cn: 由此而生：事后存在的分支，以及在其中工作却无完整成员身份的人。

branches.en: NAME WITHOUT OWNERSHIP: a partner that sells for another and keeps its own till.
branches.cn: 有名无属：替别人卖货、却用自己的收银机的伙伴。

branches.en: TWO KINDS OF FLAG: the label of attached status, and the local station that flies a national name.
branches.cn: 两种旗号：附属身份的标签，以及挂着全国名号的地方台。

intro.en: Affiliate is built on the Latin word for a son, and the same pieces build its whole noun and adjective family.
intro.cn: affiliate 建在拉丁语表示「儿子」的词上，同一批构件构成了它整个名词与形容词词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin filius and the prefix ad- produce affiliate, affiliation, affiliated and filial; the endings mark agent, state and quality.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 filius 与前缀 ad- 构成 affiliate、affiliation、affiliated 与 filial；各词尾分别标示施事、状态与性质。

items.example: The prefix directs the attachment toward a parent body.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把归属朝向母机构。

items.example: The root supplies the image of being taken into a family.
items.exampleCN: 词根提供「被纳入家庭」的意象。

items.example: The verb first named adoption, then institutional attachment.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词先指收养，后指机构归属。

items.example: The station became an affiliate of the network.
items.exampleCN: 这家电台成为该联播网的附属台。

items.example: Please state your institutional affiliation.
items.exampleCN: 请写明你的所属机构。

items.example: The affiliated colleges share one examination board.
items.exampleCN: 附属学院共用一个考试委员会。

items.example: Unaffiliated scholars may apply for the grant.
items.exampleCN: 无所属机构的学者也可申请这笔资助。

items.example: Filial duty kept him near his mother.
items.exampleCN: 子女的责任让他守在母亲身边。

items.meaning: the relation of child to parent
items.example: The abbey recorded its filiation in a charter.
items.exampleCN: 这座修道院在特许状中记下了自己的源流。
