definition_zh: 会员身份；全体会员；会员人数；会费；会籍；成员关系；集合的属于关系；会员制
definition_en: the state of belonging to a group, or the members of a group taken together
core_image: 一张塑料会员卡，边缘磨得发白，卡号处有一道被反复摩挲的指印
scene: 旧图书馆的借书台前，管理员把一张磨旧的卡片推回来，说补缴费用后名字才会重新留在名册上。At the old library desk the clerk pushed back a worn card and said her membership would be renewed once the fee was paid.
sceneCN: 这里 membership 指「会员身份」（第 1 个义项：某人作为会员的资格）；句意为管理员把磨旧的卡片推回来，说补缴费用后她的会员身份才会续上。可辨识物件：借书台、磨白的卡片、名册、印章。

pos.zh: 会员身份；全体会员；会员人数；会费；会籍；成员关系；（数学）属于关系；会员制

derivatives.zh: 复合名词：由会员身份与卡片合成的会员卡，用来证明身份

senses.title: A place on the roll
senses.definition: the state of being a member of a group or organization
senses.definitionCN: 作为某团体或组织的成员而具有的身份
senses.example: Membership gives you a vote at the annual meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 会员身份让你在年会上拥有投票权。
senses.why: The suffix -ship names a condition rather than a person: a member is who you are, and membership is the standing that follows.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ship 命名的是状态而非人：成员是你是「谁」，而会员身份是随之而来的地位。

senses.title: Everyone on the roll
senses.definition: the members of an organization considered as one group
senses.definitionCN: 作为一个整体来看的某组织的全体成员
senses.example: The whole membership was invited to the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 全体会员都应邀参加了投票。
senses.why: A collective noun is a short step from the state: if everyone holds the status, the status can name everyone.
senses.whyCN: 从状态到集体名词只差一步：如果人人都拥有这个身份，这个身份就可以用来指所有人。

senses.title: The number counted
senses.definition: the total number of members in a body
senses.definitionCN: 某组织的成员总人数
senses.example: Membership fell below two hundred last year.
senses.exampleCN: 去年会员人数降到了两百以下。
senses.why: Once a roll exists it can be counted, and the abstract noun takes on a number.
senses.whyCN: 名册一旦存在就可以清点，这个抽象名词于是带上了数字。

senses.title: The fee on the counter
senses.definition: the amount paid regularly in order to remain a member
senses.definitionCN: 为保留成员身份而定期缴纳的费用
senses.example: The annual membership is due in January.
senses.exampleCN: 年度会费在一月到期缴纳。
senses.why: Institutions turned the status into something sold by the year, and the price borrowed the name of what it bought.
senses.whyCN: 机构把身份变成按年出售的东西，价格便借用了它所购买之物的名字。

senses.title: The term of the card
senses.definition: the period during which a person's status as a member lasts
senses.definitionCN: 一个人的成员身份持续的那段时间
senses.example: She let her membership lapse after the move.
senses.exampleCN: 搬家之后，她的会籍就中断了。
senses.why: A status that can be renewed must also have an end, so the noun covers the span as well as the state.
senses.whyCN: 可以续期的身份也必然有终点，因此这个名词既指状态，也指那段时间。

senses.title: One body inside another
senses.definition: the position of a state or organization as a member of a larger body
senses.definitionCN: 国家或组织作为更大机构成员的地位
senses.example: Membership in the union requires unanimous consent.
senses.exampleCN: 加入该联盟需要全体一致同意。
senses.why: The word leaves persons behind: whole countries can hold membership in a body above them.
senses.whyCN: 这个词越过了个人：整个国家也能在更高一级的机构中拥有成员地位。

senses.title: Belonging to a set
senses.definition: in mathematics, the relation of an element to the set that contains it
senses.definitionCN: 数学中元素与其所属集合之间的关系
senses.example: The proof rests on the membership of every point in the interval.
senses.exampleCN: 这个证明依赖于区间内每一点都属于该集合。
senses.why: Logic needed a precise word for one thing being inside another, and borrowed the everyday noun.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学需要一个精确的说法来表示一物处在另一物之中，于是借用了这个日常名词。

senses.title: Sold as a scheme
senses.titleCN: 作为制度出售的会员资格
senses.definition: used before another noun for a paid scheme that grants member benefits
senses.definitionCN: 用在另一名词前，指授予会员权益的付费制度
senses.example: The store pushed its membership programme in every aisle.
senses.exampleCN: 这家商店在每条过道里推销它的会员制度。
senses.why: Commerce compressed the whole relationship into a label, and the label itself became a product.
senses.whyCN: 商业把整段关系压缩成一个标签，而标签本身又成了商品。

intro.en: Membership joins member, from Latin membrum 'limb, part', to the Old English suffix -scipe 'state, condition'. Latin had already extended the limb word to a person who is a part of a body. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: membership 由 member 加古英语后缀 -scipe（表状态、身份）构成；member 来自拉丁 membrum「肢体、部分」。拉丁语已把这个指肢体的词扩展到「作为一个机体之部分的人」。下列年代均为约数。

items.en: Membrum meant a limb or a part of the body, and Latin writers extended it to persons as parts of a community. Its deeper origin is generally thought to involve a root for cutting, but that account is a reconstruction rather than a proven form.
items.cn: membrum 意为肢体或身体的一部分，拉丁作者已把它扩展到「共同体之部分的个人」。其更深来源一般被认为与表示「切割」的词根有关，但该说法属重构，并非已证形式。

items.en: -scipe formed nouns of state and condition, as in freondscipe 'friendship'. It is generally thought to be connected with the verb for shaping or creating, and it is the direct source of the modern suffix.
items.cn: -scipe 构成表状态与身份的名词，如 freondscipe「友谊」。它一般被认为与表示「塑造、创造」的动词有关，是现代后缀的直接来源。

items.en: English borrowed membre from Old French in the thirteenth century, and the -b- spelling settled later under Latin influence.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪从古法语借入 membre，拼写中的 -b- 后来在拉丁语影响下固定下来。

items.en: From the sixteenth century member and -ship combined for the state of being a member. The collective sense and the fee sense followed in later commercial use.
items.cn: 从十六世纪起，member 与 -ship 组合表示成员身份。集体义与会费义在此后的商业用法中相继出现。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root and first date): the root of membrum is a reconstruction, and the first use of the combined noun is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根与首见年代）：membrum 的词根属重构，这个组合名词的首见年代也无确切记录。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root words and two near look-alikes whose roots are unrelated; group two holds the words for belonging to an organization.
note.cn: 第一组是同根词，另加两个字形相近却词根无关的词；第二组是表示「归属于某组织」的词。

entries.definition: The person on the roll; membership is the standing that person holds, not the person.
entries.definitionCN: 名册上的那个人；membership 是此人所拥有的身份，而不是人本身。

entries.definition: To cut off the limbs of a body, built on the limb sense; it has nothing to do with lists of members.
entries.definitionCN: 切去肢体，建在「肢体」这一义上；它与成员名单毫无关系。

entries.definition: Built on memor 'mindful', not on membrum: it means the act of recalling, despite the similar sound.
entries.definitionCN: 建在 memor「留心的」之上而非 membrum：意为回忆，尽管读音相近。

entries.definition: Shares only the -ship ending; the base is champion, from Latin campus by way of a contest in a field.
entries.definitionCN: 只共用 -ship 后缀；基础词是 champion，经「场地上的竞技」这一路径上溯到拉丁 campus。

entries.definition: A formal connection with a body, often only a listed institution; membership carries rights, dues and a place on the roll.
entries.definitionCN: 与某机构的正式联系，常只是登记一个所属单位；membership 则含权利、会费与名册上的位置。

entries.definition: An organized group of people, or the act of joining; membership is the status inside such a group.
entries.definitionCN: 有组织的人群团体，或加入这一团体的行为；membership 是身处其中的身份。

entries.definition: The payment that keeps a service or publication coming; membership may involve a subscription, but it also grants a status.
entries.definitionCN: 维持服务或刊物送达的付款；membership 可能包含订阅费，但它还授予一种身份。

entries.definition: The act of registering on a course or list; membership is the state that follows enrolment.
entries.definitionCN: 在课程或名单上登记的行为；membership 是登记之后持续的状态。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin limb word, the real suffix of state, and the real phrases used on forms and at counters.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁「肢体」词、真实的状态后缀，以及表格与柜台上真实使用的搭配。

normal.en: Member is a limb of a body, and a member is a limb of an organization: the same picture at two scales.
normal.cn: 成员是团体的「肢体」，也是组织的「一肢」：同一幅图在两个尺度上重复。

normal.en: The suffix -ship works the same way in friendship, hardship and membership: it turns a base into a state.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ship 在 friendship、hardship 与 membership 中作用相同：把基础词变成一种状态。

normal.en: Forms say membership card and membership fee, which is where most people meet the word.
normal.cn: 表格上写会员卡与会费，多数人正是从这里认识这个词。

normal.en: A life membership lasts as long as the person; an annual one must be renewed.
normal.cn: 终身会员资格持续到人离世，年度会籍则必须续期。

normal.en: The plural memberships covers several separate memberships held at once.
normal.cn: 复数 memberships 指同时持有的几份会员资格。

abstract.en: Picture a card worn pale at the edges because a thumb has checked it at the door for years.
abstract.cn: 想象一张卡片边缘被磨得发白，因为多年来在门口被拇指反复核对。

abstract.en: Picture a roll on the wall with a tick beside each name, and one line left blank.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上的一份名册，每个名字旁有一个勾，只留一行空白。

abstract.en: Picture a country's flag hung inside a larger hall, one flag among many.
abstract.cn: 想象一个国家的旗子挂在一座更大的会堂里，众多旗子中的一面。

examples.en: Membership in the society is open to anyone who applies.
examples.cn: 该学会的会员资格向所有申请者开放。

examples.en: The club raised its membership fee by ten percent.
examples.cn: 这家俱乐部把会费提高了百分之十。

examples.en: Total membership has doubled since the new branch opened.
examples.cn: 自新分部开设以来，会员总数翻了一倍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「member（成员）+ ship（船）」——一张船票把你载进名册 → 会员身份、会籍

root: member（拉丁 membrum「肢体、部分」，引申为团体之一员）+ 古英语 -scipe（表状态、身份）；「肢体属于身体」→「人属于团体」。membrum 更深词根属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one card: the standing it proves, the whole roll behind it, the number on that roll, the fee that keeps the name there, the term before renewal, a body that holds membership in a larger body, an element inside a set, and the paid scheme that sells the whole arrangement.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一张卡片展开：卡片所证明的身份、卡片背后的整份名册、名册上的人数、让名字留在名册上的会费、续期之前的期限、一个机构在更大机构中的成员地位、集合中的元素关系，以及把整套安排当作商品出售的会员制。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plastic card worn pale at the edges, checked at the door for years.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张边缘磨白的塑料卡片，多年来在门口被反复核对。

branches.en: STATE AND TERM: a place on the roll, and the span of time for which the card stays valid.
branches.cn: 身份与期限：名册上的一个位置，以及卡片保持有效的那段时间。

branches.en: THE ROLL AND ITS COUNT: the members taken together, and the number they add up to.
branches.cn: 名册与清点：合在一起看的全体成员，以及他们累计出的人数。

branches.en: THE PRICE OF THE CARD: the fee that keeps the name on the roll.
branches.cn: 卡片的价格：让名字留在名册上的那笔会费。

branches.en: BODY INSIDE BODY: a state or organization holding membership in a larger union.
branches.cn: 机构之中的机构：国家或组织在更大联盟中的成员地位。

branches.en: LOGIC AND COMMERCE: belonging to a set, and the paid scheme that sells the status.
branches.cn: 逻辑与商业：元素属于集合，以及把身份当作商品出售的会员制。

intro.en: Membership is member plus a suffix of state, and member itself goes back to the Latin word for a limb.
intro.cn: membership 是 member 加一个表状态的后缀，而 member 本身可上溯到拉丁语表示「肢体」的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin membrum gives member; Old English -scipe gives the modern -ship, and -s marks the plural. The Latin word has no verb in this family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 membrum 给出 member；古英语 -scipe 给出今天的 -ship，-s 标示复数。这个拉丁词在这一词族中没有对应的动词。

items.example: The Latin noun is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词是整个词族的基础。

items.structure: membrum + -er (English form of the Latin noun)
items.example: Each member of the team signed the card.
items.exampleCN: 队里的每一名成员都签了卡片。

items.example: The members voted on the proposal.
items.exampleCN: 成员们对这项提案进行了表决。

items.example: Membership gives you a vote at the annual meeting.
items.exampleCN: 会员身份让你在年会上拥有投票权。

items.example: He holds memberships in two learned societies.
items.exampleCN: 他在两个学会都拥有会员资格。

items.example: Nonmembers pay a higher entrance fee.
items.exampleCN: 非会员需付更高的入场费。

items.meaning: to cut off the limbs of a body
items.example: The old penalty was to dismember the body.
items.exampleCN: 古代的刑罚是把身体肢解。

items.meaning: the act or result of cutting apart
items.example: The chronicle records the dismemberment of the kingdom.
items.exampleCN: 编年史记下了王国的分裂。

definition_zh: 成员；会员；成员国；肢体；议员；集合元素；构件；家庭成员
definition_en: one of the parts or people that make up a group or a body
core_image: 一张长桌四周坐满人，每把椅子背后贴着写了名字的纸牌
scene: 点名时秘书念出一个名字，长桌尽头有人举手，墙上的名册随即在那一行后面打了一个勾。As the secretary read the roll, a hand went up at the far end of the table, and the list on the wall received a tick beside that member.
sceneCN: 这里 member 指「团体中的一名成员」（第 1 个义项）；句意为点名时长桌尽头有人举手应到，墙上的名册在该成员那一行打勾。可辨识物件：长桌、名册、铅笔、举起的手。

pos.zh: 成员；会员；成员国；肢体；议员；集合元素；构件；家庭成员
成员的；作定语的（如成员国）

derivatives.zh: 会员身份（member + -ship，由「人」转为「身份」）
肢解；切去肢体（dis- + member，由「肢体」义派生）

senses.title: One among many
senses.definition: a person who belongs to a group, team or organization
senses.definitionCN: 属于某团体、队伍或组织的一个人
senses.example: Every member of the team signed the card.
senses.exampleCN: 队里的每一名成员都签了卡片。
senses.why: The Latin word for a limb was applied to people as parts of a community, and this is the sense that dominates today.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语指「肢体」的词被用来指共同体中的个人，这成了今天最主要的义项。

senses.title: A state among states
senses.definition: a country or organization that belongs to a larger union
senses.definitionCN: 属于更大联盟的国家或组织
senses.example: The member states met to revise the treaty.
senses.exampleCN: 各成员国开会修订这项条约。
senses.why: Once a body can be a part of a larger body, whole states take the name that once belonged to persons.
senses.whyCN: 既然一个机构可以是更大机构的一部分，整个国家也就用上了原属个人的称呼。

senses.title: A limb of the body
senses.definition: an arm, leg or other part of the body
senses.definitionCN: 手臂、腿或身体的其他部位
senses.example: The old anatomy text speaks of the body and its members.
senses.exampleCN: 那本古老的解剖学著作谈到身体及其四肢。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer: the Latin noun named a limb before it named a person in a group.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层：这个拉丁名词先指肢体，后指团体中的人。

senses.title: A seat in the house
senses.definition: a person elected or appointed to a legislative assembly
senses.definitionCN: 经选举或任命进入立法机构的个人
senses.example: The member for the northern district spoke last.
senses.exampleCN: 北部选区的议员最后发言。
senses.why: Legislatures borrow the plain word for a group member and make it a title with a constituency attached.
senses.whyCN: 立法机构借用这个表示团体成员的普通词，并给它加上选区，使之成为头衔。

senses.title: An element of a set
senses.definition: an object that belongs to a mathematical set
senses.definitionCN: 属于某一数学集合的对象
senses.example: Each member of the set shares one property.
senses.exampleCN: 集合中的每个元素都共有一种性质。
senses.why: Mathematics needed a neutral word for what is inside a set, and the everyday noun was precise enough.
senses.whyCN: 数学需要一个中性词来指集合内部的东西，而这个日常名词已经足够精确。

senses.title: A part of a frame
senses.definition: one of the beams or parts that make up a structure
senses.definitionCN: 构成某一结构的梁或其他部件
senses.example: Every member of the truss carries part of the load.
senses.exampleCN: 桁架的每个构件都承担一部分荷载。
senses.why: Engineering returns to the limb sense: a frame is a body, and its beams are its members.
senses.whyCN: 工程学回到了「肢体」义：框架是一个躯体，梁就是它的肢体。

senses.title: One of the household
senses.definition: a person belonging to a family or household
senses.definitionCN: 属于某个家庭或住户的人
senses.example: The household has four members, two of them children.
senses.exampleCN: 这个家庭有四名成员，其中两名是孩子。
senses.why: The smallest group a person belongs to is a household, and the word scales down without changing.
senses.whyCN: 一个人所属的最小团体就是家庭，这个词缩小尺度而含义不变。

senses.title: One of a species group
senses.definition: an organism belonging to a particular group in taxonomy
senses.definitionCN: 在分类学上属于某一类群的生物
senses.example: This species is a member of the rose family.
senses.exampleCN: 这个物种是蔷薇科的一员。
senses.why: Natural history treats a family as a body and its species as members, completing the same metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 博物学把一个科当作躯体、把其中的物种当作成员，完成了同一个比喻。

intro.en: Member comes from Latin membrum 'limb, part of the body', which Latin also used for a person as a part of a community. English borrowed it through Old French. Its deeper origin is not settled. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: member 来自拉丁 membrum「肢体、身体的一部分」，拉丁语也用这个词指作为共同体之部分的个人。英语经古法语借入。其更深来源尚无定论。下列年代均为约数。

items.en: Membrum is well recorded for a limb. The extension to a person who is a part of a group is also Latin, not a later English invention.
items.cn: membrum 指肢体有充分书证。把它扩展到「团体之部分的个人」也发生在拉丁语中，并非英语后来的创造。

items.en: The deeper origin of membrum is generally thought to involve a root for cutting or dividing, but the form is a reconstruction and different handbooks word it differently.
items.cn: membrum 的更深来源一般被认为与表示「切割、划分」的词根有关，但该形式属重构，各家手册的表述也不一致。

items.en: Old French membre carried both the limb sense and the social sense, and English took the word in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 membre 同时带有「肢体」义与社会义，英语在十三世纪借入这个词。

items.en: From the sixteenth century the word spread to legislatures, mathematics and engineering, each borrowing the part-of-a-whole image.
items.cn: 从十六世纪起，这个词扩展到立法机构、数学与工程学，每一处都借用了「整体之一部分」的意象。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root): the pre-Latin form is a reconstruction, so the family image at the base is inferred rather than demonstrated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：前拉丁语的形式属重构，因此词底的家庭意象属推断而非实证。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root forms and one look-alike built on an unrelated root; group two holds words for people who belong to something.
note.cn: 第一组是同根形式，另加一个建在无关词根上的形近词；第二组是表示「属于某处的人」的词。

entries.definition: The status of being a member; member is the person, membership is what that person holds.
entries.definitionCN: 成员的身份；member 是人，membership 是此人所拥有的身份。

entries.definition: To cut a body into parts, built directly on the limb sense of the Latin noun.
entries.definitionCN: 把身体切成数块，直接建在这个拉丁名词的「肢体」义上。

entries.definition: From re- plus memor 'mindful', not from membrum: it means to recall, and only the sound connects it.
entries.definitionCN: 由 re- 加 memor「留心的」构成，并非来自 membrum：意为回想，只有读音把它联系起来。

entries.definition: Also from memor 'mindful'; the shared letters suggest a limb root that is not there.
entries.definitionCN: 同样来自 memor「留心的」；相同的字母让人以为有「肢体」词根，其实并没有。

entries.definition: An organization attached to a larger one; a member can be a person or a body, while an affiliate is always an organization.
entries.definitionCN: 附属于更大机构的组织；member 可以是人也可以是机构，而 affiliate 总是机构。

entries.definition: A colleague or linked firm without formal membership; a member holds a defined place on a roll.
entries.definitionCN: 无正式成员身份的同事或关联公司；member 在名册上拥有明确的位置。

entries.definition: A companion or peer, often in a learned society; fellow stresses equality, member stresses inclusion.
entries.definitionCN: 同伴或同侪，常用于学会；fellow 强调平等，member 强调被纳入。

entries.definition: A person who takes part in an event; a participant need not be on any roll, while a member is.
entries.definitionCN: 参与某项活动的人；参与者不必在名册上，而成员则在名册上。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin limb word, the real institutional compounds, and the real derived forms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁「肢体」词、真实的机构复合词，以及真实的派生形式。

normal.en: A member is a limb of the body of the group: the metaphor is the same at both scales.
normal.cn: 成员是团体的「肢体」：这个比喻在两个尺度上完全一致。

normal.en: The oldest sense is anatomical, which is why dismember means cutting off limbs, not expelling people.
normal.cn: 最古老的义项是解剖学上的，因此 dismember 指切去肢体，而不是开除成员。

normal.en: Compound phrases: member state, family member, staff member, founding member.
normal.cn: 复合搭配：成员国、家庭成员、工作人员、创始成员。

normal.en: A member of parliament is a member first and a representative second, which is why the title keeps the plain word.
normal.cn: 议会议员先是「成员」，其次才是代表，因此这个头衔保留了那个朴素的词。

normal.en: The plural is regular, and the possessive adds an apostrophe with the possessive ending.
normal.cn: 复数按常规变化，所有格则在词尾加撇号与属格标记。

abstract.en: Picture a long table where every chair has a name card taped to its back.
abstract.cn: 想象一张长桌，每把椅子背后都贴着一张写有名字的卡片。

abstract.en: Picture a truss bridge seen as a skeleton, each beam a limb holding the whole up.
abstract.cn: 想象一座桁架桥被看成一具骨架，每根梁都是撑起整体的一肢。

abstract.en: Picture a family photograph in which each face occupies one place in the frame.
abstract.cn: 想象一张全家福，每张脸都在画面里占一个位置。

examples.en: She became a member of the research group in her second year.
examples.cn: 她在第二年成为研究小组的成员。

examples.en: The member states disagreed over the wording of the clause.
examples.cn: 各成员国对条款的措辞意见不一。

examples.en: The fall injured a member of his left hand.
examples.cn: 那次跌倒伤到了他左手的一处肢体。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「member = mem（记忆）+ ber」——被记住、被写进名册的人 → 成员、会员

root: 拉丁 membrum「肢体、身体的一部分」；由「躯体之一肢」引申为「团体之一员」。更深词根属重构，不作定论。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one limb: a person on the roll, a state inside a union, the anatomical limb itself, a seat in a legislature, an element in a set, a beam in a frame, a face in a household, and a species inside a family.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕「一肢」展开：名册上的人、联盟中的国家、解剖意义上的肢体、立法机构中的一席、集合中的元素、框架中的一根梁、家庭中的一张面孔，以及一个科之内的一个物种。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long table where every chair carries a name card on its back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张长桌，每把椅子背后都贴着写有名字的卡片。

branches.en: PERSONS AND HOUSEHOLDS: the person on the roll, and the smallest group that person belongs to.
branches.cn: 个人与家庭：名册上的人，以及此人所归属的最小团体。

branches.en: STATES AND UNIONS: a whole country holding a place inside a larger body.
branches.cn: 国家与联盟：整个国家在更大机构中占据一席。

branches.en: THE OLDEST LAYER: the limb itself, the literal body part behind the metaphor.
branches.cn: 最古老的一层：肢体本身，也就是比喻背后那个字面的身体部位。

branches.en: THE SEAT IN THE HOUSE: a legislator whose title keeps the plain word for a group member.
branches.cn: 议会中的一席：立法者的头衔保留了「团体成员」这个朴素说法。

branches.en: PARTS OF STRUCTURED WHOLE: a set element, a structural beam, and a species inside a family.
branches.cn: 结构整体的各个部分：集合元素、结构构件，以及一个科之内的物种。

intro.en: Member is the Latin limb word reshaped in English, and its family runs from anatomy to institutions.
intro.cn: member 是拉丁语「肢体」一词在英语中的变形，其词族从解剖学一直延伸到制度。

latinIntro.en: Latin membrum yields member and dismember; -ship and non- build the social forms. The Latin noun is third-declension in -um, not a verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 membrum 衍生出 member 与 dismember；-ship 与 non- 构成社会义的形式。这个拉丁名词属 -um 第二变格法，并非动词。

items.example: The Latin noun is the base of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词是词族的基础。

items.example: Every member of the team signed the card.
items.exampleCN: 队里的每一名成员都签了卡片。

items.example: The members voted on the proposal.
items.exampleCN: 成员们对这项提案进行了表决。

items.example: Membership carries the right to vote.
items.exampleCN: 会员身份带有投票权。

items.example: Nonmembers may visit on weekdays only.
items.exampleCN: 非会员只能在工作日参观。

items.example: The old chronicle describes how they dismembered the statue.
items.exampleCN: 那部旧编年史描述了人们如何把雕像肢解。

items.meaning: the act or result of cutting apart
items.example: The treaty led to the dismemberment of the kingdom.
items.exampleCN: 这项条约导致王国被分裂。

items.example: The member state blocked the proposal.
items.exampleCN: 该成员国否决了这项提案。

definition_zh: 归属感；随身物品；所属状态；亲密依恋；成员身份；归属之地；被接纳；所有权归属
definition_en: the feeling of being accepted, or the things that belong to a person
core_image: 一只旧木箱里，最上面压着一条洗到发灰的毯子
scene: 搬家那天，孩子把一条旧毯子放在箱子最上面，说到了新住处也要把它摆在床头。On moving day the child laid an old blanket on top of the box and said it would carry a sense of belonging into the new flat.
sceneCN: 这里 belonging 指「归属感」（第 1 个义项）；句意为孩子把旧毯子放在箱子最上面，说要把这份归属感带进新住处。可辨识物件：纸箱、旧毯子、胶带、新房的钥匙。

pos.zh: 归属感；随身物品；所属状态；亲密依恋；成员身份；归属之地；被接纳；所有权归属

derivatives.zh: 随身物品（belonging + -s，由「属于某人的东西」转为「随身之物」）
归属需要；归属感（belonging + -ness，心理学术语）

senses.title: The feeling of being accepted
senses.definition: the feeling of being accepted and secure within a group
senses.definitionCN: 在某个群体中被接纳、感到安稳的体验
senses.example: A sense of belonging matters more than a good salary to many workers.
senses.exampleCN: 对许多劳动者来说，归属感比一份好薪水更重要。
senses.why: Psychology took the plain verb and made a noun of feeling: not where a person is listed, but how being listed feels.
senses.whyCN: 心理学把这个朴素的动词变成表示感受的名词：不是一个人被登记在哪里，而是被登记的感受如何。

senses.title: The things in the case
senses.definition: the personal possessions that a person carries or owns
senses.definitionCN: 一个人随身携带或拥有的私人物品
senses.example: She packed her belongings into two cases.
senses.exampleCN: 她把随身物品装进了两个箱子。
senses.why: What belongs to a person is, in the plural, simply what that person has; the abstract noun turns concrete.
senses.whyCN: 属于一个人的东西，用复数来说，就是此人所拥有的东西；抽象名词由此变得具体。

senses.title: The part and the whole
senses.definition: the state of being a part or a property of something larger
senses.definitionCN: 作为更大事物的一部分或一种属性的状态
senses.example: The belonging of the manuscript to the abbey is documented.
senses.exampleCN: 这份手稿归属于修道院一事有文献为证。
senses.why: The noun names the relation itself, apart from the person or body that holds it.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名的是关系本身，与持有它的个人或机构分开来看。

senses.title: The close tie
senses.definition: a close and affectionate relationship between people
senses.definitionCN: 人与人之间亲近而深厚的感情联系
senses.example: There was a belonging between the two cousins that needed no words.
senses.exampleCN: 两位表亲之间有一种无需言语的亲密联结。
senses.why: The same word covers attachment to a place and attachment to a person, because both are forms of being held.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词既指对地方的依恋，也指对人的依恋，因为两者都是「被牵住」的形式。

senses.title: The name on the roll
senses.definition: the status of being a member of a body
senses.definitionCN: 作为某机构成员的身份
senses.example: Her belonging to the choir lasted thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 她在唱诗班的成员身份持续了三十年。
senses.why: Membership is the institutional face of the same relation, and the noun can name it without the suffix -ship.
senses.whyCN: 成员身份是同一关系在制度层面的面貌，这个词不用那个表身份的后缀也能命名它。

senses.title: The place called home
senses.definition: the place or community where a person feels at home
senses.definitionCN: 一个人感到自在如归的地方或社群
senses.example: The old square still gives him a sense of belonging.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老广场仍然给他一种归属感。
senses.why: Attachment to a place is not a possession and not a membership, yet the word covers it because the place holds the person.
senses.whyCN: 对地方的依恋既不是所有物，也不是成员身份，但这个词仍涵盖它，因为地方「牵住」了人。

senses.title: Accepted by the group
senses.definition: the inclusion of a newcomer in a group by the group itself
senses.definitionCN: 群体主动把新来者纳入其中
senses.example: The school worked hard on the belonging of transfer students.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校努力让转学生获得接纳。
senses.why: The feeling in sense one needs a cause on the other side: someone must do the accepting.
senses.whyCN: 第一个义项里的感受需要一个来自他方的成因：必须有人做出接纳。

senses.title: Owned in law
senses.definition: the state of being legally owned by a person or body
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上为某个人或机构所有的状态
senses.example: The belonging of the islands was disputed for a century.
senses.exampleCN: 这些岛屿的归属争议持续了一个世纪。
senses.why: Courts need a neutral noun for who holds title, and the everyday word serves without technical trim.
senses.whyCN: 法庭需要一个中性名词来指谁持有产权，这个日常词无需技术加工即可胜任。

intro.en: Belonging is the verb belong with the noun suffix -ing. Belong comes from Middle English belongen, be- added to longen 'to pertain'. The origin of longen is uncertain, and the word has no Latin cognates. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: belonging 是动词 belong 加名词后缀 -ing 构成。belong 来自中古英语 belongen，由 be- 加 longen「属于、相关」构成。longen 的来源不确定，这个词也没有拉丁同族词。下列年代均为约数。

items.en: The verb is recorded from the fourteenth century as belongen, with be- added to longen 'to pertain'. The earliest citation is not firmly dated.
items.cn: 这个动词在十四世纪以 belongen 的形式出现，由 be- 加 longen「属于、相关」构成。最早书证没有确切年代。

items.en: Longen is generally thought to be related to Old English langian 'to pertain' and to gelang 'dependent on', though the exact relation is debated.
items.cn: longen 一般被认为与古英语 langian「属于、相关」及 gelang「取决于」有关，但确切关系仍有争论。

items.en: The word is native English and has no Latin relatives, so any Latin-looking root explanation is a guess rather than a derivation.
items.cn: 这个词是英语本族词，没有拉丁同族，因此任何看似拉丁词根的解释都只是猜测，而非派生。

items.en: The -ing noun appeared later, first for possessions and then, in modern psychology, for the feeling of acceptance.
items.cn: 带 -ing 的名词出现较晚，先指所有物，后来在现代心理学中指被接纳的感受。

items.en: Source uncertain (origin and first date): the pre-history of longen is unsettled, several explanations compete, and none is adopted here.
items.cn: 来源不确定（来源与首见年代）：longen 的早期历史没有定论，数种解释并存，此处不选定论。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root forms and two words that merely end alike; group two holds the words for being attached to people, places and groups.
note.cn: 第一组是同根形式，另加两个只是词尾相似的词；第二组是表示「对人、地方与群体有所依附」的词。

entries.definition: The verb behind the noun; belonging names the state or the things, while belong names the relation in action.
entries.definitionCN: 名词背后的动词；belonging 指状态或物品，而 belong 指处于活动中的关系。

entries.definition: The plural is fixed for personal possessions; the singular names feelings and relations, not things.
entries.definitionCN: 复数固定指个人物品；单数则指感受与关系，不指东西。

entries.definition: From a word for a deep roar, probably imitative; only the ending resembles belonging.
entries.definitionCN: 来自一个表示低沉吼叫的词，很可能是拟声词；只有词尾与 belonging 相似。

entries.definition: From the verb build plus -ing, with no relation to belong; the shared pattern is the noun ending alone.
entries.definitionCN: 由表示「建造」的动词加 -ing 构成，与 belong 无关；共同之处仅在名词词尾。

entries.definition: Any bond, physical or emotional; belonging is the bond that comes from being accepted or from owning.
entries.definitionCN: 任何联结，无论实体还是情感；belonging 是由被接纳或拥有而来的联结。

entries.definition: A natural attraction or resemblance; belonging implies a place one holds, not merely a likeness.
entries.definitionCN: 天生的吸引或相似；belonging 意味着一个人所拥有的位置，而不只是相似。

entries.definition: Membership is the formal status with rights and dues; belonging can be a feeling with no card at all.
entries.definitionCN: membership 是带权利与会费的正式身份；belonging 可以只是一种感受，连卡片都没有。

entries.definition: The act or policy of including people; belonging is the resulting sense of being inside.
entries.definitionCN: 把人纳入的行为或政策；belonging 是随之而来的「身在其中」的感受。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real native verb, the real plural for possessions, and the real psychological term built on it.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的本族动词、真实表示物品的复数形式，以及由它构成的真实心理学术语。

normal.en: Belong plus -ing turns a relation into a thing you can feel or pack: a sense of belonging, or belongings in a case.
normal.cn: belong 加 -ing 把一种关系变成可感、可打包的东西：归属感，或箱子里的随身物品。

normal.en: The plural belongings is fixed and concrete; the singular is abstract and emotional.
normal.cn: 复数 belongings 固定而具体；单数则抽象而带情感。

normal.en: Belongingness is the psychologist's name for the need to be accepted, built by adding -ness to belonging.
normal.cn: belongingness 是心理学家给「被接纳的需要」起的名字，由 belonging 加 -ness 构成。

normal.en: The verb has no Latin ancestry, which is why no Latin root is offered for it.
normal.cn: 这个动词没有拉丁渊源，因此不为其编造拉丁词根。

normal.en: Common phrases: a sense of belonging, personal belongings, a feeling of belonging.
normal.cn: 常见搭配：归属感、个人随身物品、归属的感受。

abstract.en: Picture a blanket laid on top of everything else in the box, so it is the first thing seen on opening.
abstract.cn: 想象一条毯子压在箱内所有东西之上，开箱时第一眼就看见它。

abstract.en: Picture a name tag on a classroom chair, waiting for the child who will sit there.
abstract.cn: 想象教室椅背上的一张名牌，等着将要坐下的孩子。

abstract.en: Picture a key that opens a door in a building where nobody asks who you are.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙，能打开一栋楼里的一扇门，而那里没人问你身份。

examples.en: A sense of belonging is strongest where names are known.
examples.cn: 在人们彼此知道名字的地方，归属感最强。

examples.en: He gathered his belongings and left the room.
examples.cn: 他收好随身物品，离开了房间。

examples.en: The belonging of the archive to the city was never in doubt.
examples.cn: 该档案馆归城市所有这一点从未有过疑问。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「be（是）+ long（长久）+ ing」——长久地待在一个地方、被那里接纳 → 归属感

root: belong（中古英语 belongen，be- + longen「属于」）+ -ing（名词后缀）；由「属于」的动作转为「归属」的状态与感受。longen 来源不确定，无拉丁同族。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one blanket in a box: the feeling of acceptance, the packed possessions, the part-whole relation, the close tie between people, the name on a roll, the place called home, the act of accepting newcomers, and legal ownership.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕箱子里的一条毯子展开：被接纳的感受、装箱的随身物品、部分与整体的关系、人与人之间的亲密联结、名册上的名字、称为家的地方、接纳新来者的行为，以及法律上的所有权。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a worn blanket laid on top of everything in the box.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条磨旧的毯子压在箱内所有东西之上。

branches.en: FELT AND GRANTED: the feeling of acceptance, and the act of accepting that produces it.
branches.cn: 感受与给予：被接纳的感受，以及产生这种感受的接纳行为。

branches.en: WHAT IS PACKED: the personal possessions that belong to a person.
branches.cn: 装箱之物：属于某个人的私人物品。

branches.en: THE RELATION ITSELF: being a part of something, and the formal membership that records it.
branches.cn: 关系本身：作为某物的一部分，以及记录这一点的正式成员身份。

branches.en: THE CLOSE TIE: attachment between people that needs no document.
branches.cn: 亲密联结：人与人之间无需文书证明的依恋。

branches.en: HELD BY PLACE OR LAW: the place where one feels at home, and ownership that a court can confirm.
branches.cn: 被地方或法律持有：让人自在如归的地方，以及法庭可以确认的所有权。

intro.en: Belonging is built from native English pieces only: a prefix, an old verb and a noun ending.
intro.cn: belonging 完全由英语本族构件构成：一个前缀、一个古老动词和一个名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Belong has no Latin cognates, so no Latin entries are offered. Its parts are be-, the Middle English verb longen 'to pertain', and -ing.
latinIntro.cn: belong 没有拉丁同族词，因此不列拉丁词条。其构件是 be-、中古英语动词 longen「属于」以及 -ing。

items.structure: be- (English prefix, here forming a verb)
items.example: The prefix turns the old verb into the modern belong.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把古老动词变成今天的 belong。

items.meaning: to pertain; to go along with
items.example: The Middle English verb supplies the core meaning.
items.exampleCN: 这个中古英语动词提供核心含义。

items.meaning: to be the property of; to have a proper place
items.example: This coat belongs to my brother.
items.exampleCN: 这件外套属于我哥哥。

items.meaning: belongs, for he or she or it
items.example: The book belongs on the top shelf.
items.exampleCN: 这本书应放在最上层。

items.example: The land belonged to the abbey for centuries.
items.exampleCN: 这片土地数百年间归修道院所有。

items.meaning: the state of belonging; a sense of acceptance
items.example: The children found a sense of belonging in the choir.
items.exampleCN: 孩子们在唱诗班里找到了归属感。

items.meaning: the things a person owns and carries
items.example: She packed her belongings into two cases.
items.exampleCN: 她把随身物品装进了两个箱子。

items.example: The study measured belongingness in new employees.
items.exampleCN: 这项研究测量了新员工的归属感。

items.meaning: a person with formal local status
items.meaningCN: 具有正式属地身份的人
items.example: The law distinguishes belongers from residents.
items.exampleCN: 法律把属地身份者与一般居民区分开来。

definition_zh: 属于；归某人所有；应在（某处）；归入（某类）；是成员；相配；应归（某人）；属于（某时代）
definition_en: to be the property of someone, or to have a proper place
core_image: 还书车上，一本书被人拿起又放下，最后被插回最下层的空位
scene: 归还台前，管理员指着最下层书架，说这本书不该放在这儿。At the return desk the librarian pointed to the lowest shelf and said the book did not belong there.
sceneCN: 这里 belong 指「应在某处」（第 2 个义项：某物应放置的位置）；句意为管理员指着最下层书架，说这本书不该放在那里。可辨识物件：还书车、书架、书脊标签、管理员的手。

pos.zh: 属于；归某人所有；应在（某处）；归入（某类）；是成员；相配；应归（某人）；属于（某时代）

collocations.zh: 不该在这里；不属于这里

derivatives.zh: 归属感；归属（belong + -ing，由动作转为状态）
随身物品（belonging + -s，指属于某人的东西）

senses.title: It is mine, not yours
senses.definition: to be the property of a person or body
senses.definitionCN: 为某个人或机构所拥有
senses.example: This coat belongs to my brother.
senses.exampleCN: 这件外套是我哥哥的。
senses.why: The oldest recorded use is possession: a thing is held by a person, and the verb states that holding.
senses.whyCN: 有记录的最早用法是所有权：一物由某人持有，这个动词陈述这种持有关系。

senses.title: It goes on that shelf
senses.definition: to have a proper or usual place
senses.definitionCN: 拥有恰当或通常的位置
senses.example: The dictionary belongs on the top shelf.
senses.exampleCN: 这本词典应放在最上层。
senses.why: From ownership the verb widened to placement: a thing belongs where it is normally kept, owner or not.
senses.whyCN: 从所有权出发，这个动词扩展到位置：一物属于它通常被放置的地方，与所有者无关。

senses.title: It falls in that class
senses.definition: to be a member of a category or class
senses.definitionCN: 属于某一类别或门类
senses.example: The fly belongs to a large order of insects.
senses.exampleCN: 这种蝇属于一个庞大的昆虫目。
senses.why: Classification treats a class as a container, and putting a thing inside it is the same gesture as putting it on a shelf.
senses.whyCN: 分类学把一个类别当作容器，把一物放进去，与把它放上书架是同一个动作。

senses.title: She is one of us
senses.definition: to be a member of a group or organization
senses.definitionCN: 是某团体或组织的成员
senses.example: She belongs to a choir that meets on Thursdays.
senses.exampleCN: 她属于一个每周四聚会的唱诗班。
senses.why: People belong to bodies as things belong to owners: the verb covers both, with the person as the possessed part.
senses.whyCN: 人属于团体，正如物属于所有者：这个动词两者都涵盖，只是此时被拥有的是人这一部分。

senses.title: These two go together
senses.definition: to suit or match something, so that the pair works as a unit
senses.definitionCN: 与某物相配，使两者成为一个整体
senses.example: That lid belongs with this jar, not with the other one.
senses.exampleCN: 那个盖子配这个罐子，不配另一个。
senses.why: Matching is placement in company: the right thing is the one that sits with its partner.
senses.whyCN: 相配就是位置上的相伴：恰当之物就是与它的伙伴坐在一起的那一个。

senses.title: The credit is hers
senses.definition: to be owed or attributed to a person as right or responsibility
senses.definitionCN: 作为权利或责任应归于某人
senses.example: The credit for the discovery belongs to the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 这项发现的功劳应归整个团队。
senses.why: Ownership becomes moral: praise, blame and duty are treated as property that has a rightful holder.
senses.whyCN: 所有权变成了道德层面的东西：赞誉、责难与责任都被当作有合法持有者的财产。

senses.title: He is of another age
senses.definition: to be characteristic of a period or setting
senses.definitionCN: 具有某个时期或环境的特征
senses.example: His manner belongs to another century.
senses.exampleCN: 他的举止属于另一个世纪。
senses.why: A person can be placed in time as an object is placed on a shelf, and the verb carries that placement.
senses.whyCN: 人可以像物件被放上书架那样被放进时间之中，这个动词承担了这种安放。

senses.title: This is where I fit
senses.definition: to feel accepted and suited to a place or group
senses.definitionCN: 感到被某地或某群体接纳并与之契合
senses.example: After a month, the new students felt they belonged.
senses.exampleCN: 一个月后，新来的学生觉得自己属于这里了。
senses.why: The verb turns inward at last: the place is not owned, but the person is held by it.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词最终转向内心：地方并未被拥有，而是人被地方所接纳。

intro.en: Belong comes from Middle English belongen, be- added to longen 'to pertain'. The origin of longen is uncertain. The word is native English and has no Latin cognates. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: belong 来自中古英语 belongen，由 be- 加 longen「属于、相关」构成。longen 的来源不确定。这个词是英语本族词，没有拉丁同族。下列年代均为约数。

items.en: The verb appears in the fourteenth century as belongen. The earliest citation is not firmly dated, and spellings vary.
items.cn: 这个动词在十四世纪以 belongen 的形式出现。最早书证没有确切年代，拼写也各不相同。

items.en: Longen is generally thought to be related to Old English langian 'to pertain' and gelang 'dependent on'. The exact relation is debated, and other explanations exist.
items.cn: longen 一般被认为与古英语 langian「属于、相关」及 gelang「取决于」有关。确切关系仍有争论，也存在其他解释。

items.en: The word is native English. No Latin relative is known, so Latin-looking roots should be treated as guesses.
items.cn: 这个词是英语本族词，没有已知的拉丁同族，因此看似拉丁词根的说法只能视为猜测。

items.en: Possession came first; placement, classification, membership and moral attribution followed by ordinary extension.
items.cn: 所有权义最先出现；位置、分类、成员身份与道德归因随后通过日常引申而来。

items.en: Source uncertain (origin and first date): the pre-history of longen is unsettled, several explanations compete, and none is adopted here.
items.cn: 来源不确定（来源与首见年代）：longen 的早期历史没有定论，数种解释并存，此处不选定论。

note.en: Group one holds the inflected and derived forms of the same verb plus two words that only sound alike; group two holds verbs for ownership and fit.
note.cn: 第一组是同一动词的屈折与派生形式，另加两个只是读音相近的词；第二组是表示「拥有」与「契合」的动词。

entries.definition: The noun of state or feeling; belong is the relation in action, belonging is what it produces.
entries.definitionCN: 表状态或感受的名词；belong 是活动中的关系，belonging 是它所产生的东西。

entries.definition: The third person singular; no separate meaning, only agreement with a singular subject.
entries.definitionCN: 第三人称单数形式；没有独立含义，只与单数主语保持一致。

entries.definition: To roar deeply, probably imitative in origin; it shares sound, not ancestry.
entries.definitionCN: 发出低沉的吼叫，来源很可能是拟声；它与 belong 只共享读音，不共享词源。

entries.definition: To swell and wave, as cloth or smoke; the resemblance is phonetic only.
entries.definitionCN: 像布或烟那样鼓起、翻卷；相似之处仅在语音。

entries.definition: To relate or be relevant to something, often in legal or formal prose; belong is the plainer everyday verb.
entries.definitionCN: 与某物相关或涉及，常用于法律或正式文体；belong 是更朴素的日常动词。

entries.definition: A formal word for belonging as a right or attribute; it never covers the feeling of fitting in.
entries.definitionCN: 作为权利或属性的正式说法；它从不涵盖「融入」的感受。

entries.definition: To be the right size or match; belong with stresses the company a thing keeps, not its measurements.
entries.definitionCN: 指尺寸合适或相配；「与……相配」这一说法强调一物与谁为伴，而非尺寸。

entries.definition: To live in a place formally; belong can place a thing or a person without any legal residence.
entries.definitionCN: 正式地居住于某地；belong 可以把物或人放进某处，不涉及法定居所。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real native verb, the real prepositional phrases, and the real derived nouns.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的本族动词、真实的介词搭配，以及真实的派生名词。

normal.en: The possession pattern is belong followed by to; the placement patterns use in and with.
normal.cn: 「属于某人」是所有权句式；「应在某处」与「与某物相配」是位置句式。

normal.en: The word is native English, so its pieces are be- and an old verb, with no Latin root to reconstruct.
normal.cn: 这个词是英语本族词，其构件是 be- 与一个古老动词，没有可重构的拉丁词根。

normal.en: Belonging is both a noun and a participle, which is why one form gives possessions and the other gives feelings.
normal.cn: belonging 既是名词也是分词，因此同一个形式既能给出随身物品，也能给出感受。

normal.en: The phrase for two things that make one set is a fixed expression meaning they should be together.
normal.cn: 「理应在一起」是固定说法，指两样东西构成一套。

normal.en: The moral sense is easy to see in the credit belongs to her.
normal.cn: 道德义在「功劳应归于她」这类句子里很容易看出。

abstract.en: Picture a book taken off a cart, weighed in the hand, and slid back into the one empty slot.
abstract.cn: 想象一本书从推车上被拿下，在手里掂了掂，又被插回唯一空着的位置。

abstract.en: Picture a child standing at the edge of a circle of players, then stepping in without being asked to leave.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子站在玩游戏的人群边上，然后迈进去，没人让他离开。

abstract.en: Picture a key hanging on a hook with a paper tag that carries the room number.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙挂在钩上，纸牌写着房间号码。

examples.en: These keys belong to the flat on the third floor.
examples.cn: 这些钥匙属于三楼的那套公寓。

examples.en: The chair belongs in the corner by the window.
examples.cn: 这把椅子应放在窗边的角落里。

examples.en: She belongs to a reading group that meets once a month.
examples.cn: 她属于一个每月聚会一次的读书小组。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「be（是）+ long（长）——长久属于一处」→ 属于、应在某处

root: 中古英语 belongen = be-（构成动词）+ longen「属于、相关」；本族词，无拉丁同族，longen 来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one book returned to its slot: possession, proper placement, classification, membership, matching company, moral attribution, a period one fits, and the inward sense of fitting in.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一本被放回原位的书展开：所有权、恰当的位置、归类、成员身份、相配的伙伴、道德上的归因、与某个时代契合，以及内心「属于这里」的感受。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a book taken off a cart and slid back into the one empty slot.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本书从推车上被拿下，又被插回唯一空着的位置。

branches.en: WHO HOLDS IT: possession in law, and credit or duty owed to a person.
branches.cn: 由谁持有：法律上的所有权，以及应归于某人的功劳或责任。

branches.en: THE RIGHT SLOT: the place where a thing is normally kept.
branches.cn: 恰当的位置：一物通常被放置的地方。

branches.en: INSIDE A CLASS: an organism or object placed within a category.
branches.cn: 类别之内：被归入某一类别的生物或物体。

branches.en: ONE OF THE GROUP: a person held by a body, as a thing is held by its owner.
branches.cn: 团体之一员：人被团体所拥有，正如物被所有者拥有。

branches.en: FITTING IN: a lid with its jar, a manner with its century, and a person with a place.
branches.cn: 契合：盖子与罐子、举止与世纪，以及人与某个地方。

intro.en: Belong is native English, built from a prefix and an old verb, and its endings are the ordinary English ones.
intro.cn: belong 是英语本族词，由一个前缀和一个古老动词构成，其词尾是常规的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: There are no Latin cognates for belong, so no Latin entries are listed. The parts are be- and the Middle English verb longen 'to pertain', with -s, -ed and -ing as endings.
latinIntro.cn: belong 没有拉丁同族词，因此不列拉丁词条。其构件是 be- 与中古英语动词 longen「属于」，词尾为 -s、-ed 与 -ing。

items.example: The prefix turns longen into the modern verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把 longen 变成今天的动词。

items.example: The old verb supplies the meaning of pertaining.
items.exampleCN: 这个古老动词提供「相关、属于」的含义。

items.meaning: to be owned by; to have a proper place
items.example: These keys belong to the flat upstairs.
items.exampleCN: 这些钥匙属于楼上那套公寓。

items.example: The chair belongs in the corner.
items.exampleCN: 这把椅子应放在角落。

items.example: The house belonged to her grandmother.
items.exampleCN: 这栋房子曾属于她的祖母。

items.meaning: being owned; the state of fitting in
items.example: The children felt they were belonging at last.
items.exampleCN: 孩子们终于觉得自己属于这里了。

items.meaning: the things a person owns and carries
items.example: He carried his belongings in one bag.
items.exampleCN: 他把随身物品装在一个包里。

items.example: The survey measured belongingness at work.
items.exampleCN: 这项调查测量了职场中的归属感。

definition_zh: 深情的；亲昵的；慈爱的；以动作表达关爱的；眷恋的；温情的；亲人（指动物）；描写温和的
definition_en: showing love or tender feeling toward someone or something
core_image: 一只手在另一只手背上轻轻拍了两下，没有说一句话
scene: 老人在门口送别孙女，抬手在她肩上拍了拍，又把围巾往上拉了拉。At the door the old man patted his granddaughter on the shoulder and pulled her scarf a little higher, an affectionate gesture that needed no words.
sceneCN: 这里 affectionate 指「以动作表达关爱的」（第 3 个义项：用举止传达爱意）；句意为老人在门口拍拍孙女的肩、替她把围巾拉高，这个动作无须言语便传达了关爱。可辨识物件：门口、围巾、抬起的手、冬日的风。

pos.zh: 深情的；亲昵的；慈爱的；以动作表达关爱的；眷恋的；温情的；亲人（指动物）；描写温和的

derivatives.zh: 喜爱；感情（affectionate 的基础名词）
深情；亲昵（affectionate + -ness，由性质转为名词）

senses.title: Loving toward a person
senses.definition: having or showing warm love for a person
senses.definitionCN: 对某人怀有或表现出温暖的爱
senses.example: She gave her father an affectionate hug at the station.
senses.exampleCN: 她在车站给了父亲一个深情的拥抱。
senses.why: The base noun names the feeling, and the ending makes it a quality that can describe a person.
senses.whyCN: 基础名词命名的是感情，词尾把这种感情变成可以形容一个人的性质。

senses.title: Tender in manner
senses.definition: tender and familiar in the way one speaks or behaves
senses.definitionCN: 说话或举止温柔而熟悉
senses.example: They exchanged affectionate nicknames that no one else used.
senses.exampleCN: 他们互相使用别人不用的亲昵称呼。
senses.why: Familiarity without warmth is only rudeness; this word adds the warmth that makes closeness visible.
senses.whyCN: 没有温度的熟稔只是随便；这个词添上了那份让亲近可见的暖意。

senses.title: Expressed by touch
senses.definition: shown through a small physical gesture rather than words
senses.definitionCN: 通过细小的身体动作而非言语来表现
senses.example: He greeted the dog with an affectionate pat on the head.
senses.exampleCN: 他拍了拍狗的头，亲切地打了招呼。
senses.why: A pat or a hand on the shoulder says what a sentence might overstate, so the adjective often attaches to gestures.
senses.whyCN: 拍一下或把手搭在肩上，能说出句子可能说得过头的话，因此这个形容词常用于动作。

senses.title: Attached to a place or thing
senses.definition: fond of a place or object in a nostalgic way
senses.definitionCN: 带着怀念地喜爱某个地方或物件
senses.example: The letter was affectionate about the old house they had sold.
senses.exampleCN: 那封信里满是对他们已卖掉的旧居的眷恋。
senses.why: The feeling can outlive the person it was first felt for and settle on the walls and the street.
senses.whyCN: 这种感情可以比最初的对象活得更久，最后落在墙壁与街道上。

senses.title: Tame with people
senses.definition: of an animal, gentle and friendly toward people
senses.definitionCN: 指动物对人温和友好
senses.example: The mare is affectionate with the children who feed her.
senses.exampleCN: 这匹母马对喂她的孩子们很亲昵。
senses.why: Animals show attachment by approach and touch, which is exactly the behaviour the human word describes.
senses.whyCN: 动物用靠近与触碰表达依恋，而这正是这个词所描述的行为。

senses.title: Warm in tone
senses.definition: warm and kind in words, letters or tone
senses.definitionCN: 言辞、书信或语气温暖和善
senses.example: His affectionate tone softened the criticism.
senses.exampleCN: 他温情的语气让批评变得柔和。
senses.why: Tone is where feeling becomes audible, and the adjective moves from the person to what the person produces.
senses.whyCN: 语气是感情变得可听的地方，这个形容词于是从人移到人的产物上。

senses.title: Fond across the years
senses.definition: remaining fond of someone through a long acquaintance
senses.definitionCN: 在长久相处中始终对某人怀有喜爱
senses.example: Their marriage remained affectionate after forty years.
senses.exampleCN: 四十年过去，他们的婚姻依然充满深情。
senses.why: The word can mark duration as well as intensity: affection that has lasted is still affection.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既可标示强度，也可标示时长：持续下来的感情仍然是感情。

senses.title: Gentle in portrayal
senses.definition: in art or writing, showing a subject with warmth rather than judgment
senses.definitionCN: 在艺术或文字中带着温情而非评判地呈现对象
senses.example: The portrait is affectionate rather than flattering.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅肖像温和亲切，却不谄媚。
senses.why: A painter can hold a person the way a relative does, and criticism borrowed the same adjective.
senses.whyCN: 画家可以像亲属那样看待一个人，评论文字便借用了同一个形容词。

intro.en: Affectionate is affection plus the Latin ending -atus. Affection comes from Latin affectio, from afficere 'to affect', built on ad- 'to' and facere 'to do, make'. The English adjective is recorded from the seventeenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: affectionate 是 affection 加拉丁词尾 -atus 构成。affection 来自拉丁 affectio，出自动词 afficere「影响、使动」，由 ad-「朝向」与 facere「做、造」构成。这个英语形容词自十七世纪起有书证。下列年代均为约数。

items.en: Facere 'to do, make' is securely recorded and has many derived words. Its deeper origin is generally thought to involve a root for placing or putting, but the form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: facere「做、造」书证确凿，派生词众多。其更深来源一般被认为与表示「放置」的词根有关，但该形式属重构。

items.en: Afficere meant to do something to a person, and so to move or influence them, whether pleasantly or painfully. The prefix ad- supplies direction.
items.cn: afficere 意为对某人做某事，因而使其动情或受影响，无论愉快还是痛苦。前缀 ad- 提供方向。

items.en: Affectio named a disposition or a state of feeling. It is the direct source of English affection, and the ending marks a state.
items.cn: affectio 指一种倾向或情感状态。它是英语 affection 的直接来源，词尾标示状态。

items.en: Affectionate appears in English from the seventeenth century as 'having affection', and the sense of outward tenderness follows.
items.cn: affectionate 自十七世纪起在英语中出现，意为「怀有感情的」，随后又发展出外在温柔的含义。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root and first date): the root of facere is a reconstruction, and the first English citation is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根与首见年代）：facere 的词根属重构，这个英语形容词的最早书证也无确切年代。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root words plus two look-alikes built on a different prefix; group two holds adjectives for warm feeling.
note.cn: 第一组是同根词，另加两个由不同前缀构成的形近词；第二组是表示温暖情感的形容词。

entries.definition: The feeling itself; affectionate describes a person or gesture that has it.
entries.definitionCN: 指感情本身；affectionate 则形容怀有这种感情的人或动作。

entries.definition: The adverb for doing something with affection; the adjective describes the doer or the act.
entries.definitionCN: 表示带着感情地做某事的副词；形容词则描述做的人或行为。

entries.definition: Built on the same verb but means put on, insincere; warmth and pretence are opposites.
entries.definitionCN: 建在同一个动词上，却意为「做作的、不真诚的」；温情与造作恰好相反。

entries.definition: From ex- plus facere, meaning able to produce a result; it shares the base but not the prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 由 ex- 加 facere 构成，意为有效；它共用基础词，但前缀不同。

entries.definition: Simply full of love; affectionate adds gentleness of manner rather than intensity.
entries.definitionCN: 直接表示充满爱；affectionate 增添的是举止上的温柔，而非强度。

entries.definition: Having a liking for someone, often with a hint of indulgence; affectionate is warmer and more outward.
entries.definitionCN: 对某人怀有喜爱，常带一点纵容意味；affectionate 更温暖，也更外显。

entries.definition: Gentle and careful with someone's feelings; affectionate stresses love, tender stresses care.
entries.definitionCN: 对他人感受温柔小心；affectionate 强调爱，tender 强调照料。

entries.definition: Attentive to another's needs; affectionate may show itself in a hug rather than in help.
entries.definitionCN: 关注他人需要；affectionate 可能只表现为一个拥抱，而非实际帮助。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin verb for doing, the real noun affection, and the real adverb built on it.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁动词「做」、真实的名词 affection，以及由它构成的真实副词。

normal.en: Affection plus -ate gives the quality of having affection, just as fortune plus -ate gives fortunate.
normal.cn: affection 加 -ate 构成「怀有感情」的性质，正如 fortune 加 -ate 构成 fortunate。

normal.en: The Latin base is ad- plus facere 'do': to affect someone is literally to do something to them.
normal.cn: 拉丁词底是 ad- 加 facere「做」：影响某人，字面上就是对其做点什么。

normal.en: The adverb affectionately marks the manner: he spoke affectionately, he patted her affectionately.
normal.cn: 副词 affectionately 标示方式：他深情地说，他亲切地拍了拍她。

normal.en: Affected looks like this word but means insincere, so the pair is worth keeping apart.
normal.cn: affected 字形相近却意为做作，这两个词值得分清。

normal.en: Common phrases pair it with greeting, nickname, gesture and letter.
normal.cn: 常见搭配与问候、昵称、动作和书信相配。

abstract.en: Picture two hands, one patting the back of the other, no words exchanged.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手，一只在另一只手背上轻拍，没有言语。

abstract.en: Picture a scarf pulled a little higher at a doorway, a small correction against the cold.
abstract.cn: 想象门口一条围巾被往上拉了拉，一个抵御寒冷的细小动作。

abstract.en: Picture a portrait where the eyes are kind but the nose is honest.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅肖像，眼神温和，鼻子却画得如实。

examples.en: He wrote an affectionate note to his old teacher.
examples.cn: 他给年迈的老师写了一封充满温情的短笺。

examples.en: The two brothers were affectionate but never demonstrative in public.
examples.cn: 兄弟俩感情深厚，却从不在公开场合外露。

examples.en: The cat is affectionate only when the fire is lit.
examples.cn: 这只猫只在炉火点着时才亲人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「affection（感情）+ ate（充满）」——满是感情 → 深情的、亲昵的

root: 拉丁 affectio「情感、倾向」+ -ate（形容词词尾）；affectio 出自 afficere「影响」= ad-（朝向）+ facere（做、造）。facere 更深词根属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one pat on the shoulder: love for a person, a familiar manner, a gesture that speaks, fondness for an old house, an animal's friendliness, a warm tone, a long marriage, and a gentle portrait.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕肩上的一拍展开：对一个人的爱、熟稔的举止、会说话的动作、对旧居的眷恋、动物的亲昵、温情的语气、长久的婚姻，以及温和的肖像。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand patting the back of another hand, with no words exchanged.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手在另一只手背上轻拍，没有言语。

branches.en: LOVE THAT LASTS: warmth toward a person, and the same warmth after forty years.
branches.cn: 持续的爱：对一个人的温情，以及四十年后仍在的同一份温情。

branches.en: MANNER AND TONE: a familiar way of speaking, and the warmth heard in a letter.
branches.cn: 举止与语气：熟稔的说话方式，以及在书信中听得见的暖意。

branches.en: THE GESTURE: a pat that says what a sentence might overstate.
branches.cn: 动作：一拍，说出了句子可能说得过头的话。

branches.en: THE OLD HOUSE: affection that outlives its first object and settles on walls.
branches.cn: 旧居：比最初对象活得更久、落在墙壁上的感情。

branches.en: GENTLENESS IN OTHER FORMS: an animal friendly to people, and a portrait kind without flattery.
branches.cn: 其他形式的温柔：对人友好的动物，以及温和而不谄媚的肖像。

intro.en: Affectionate is built on the Latin verb for doing, and its family runs through feeling, manner and pretence.
intro.cn: affectionate 建在拉丁语表示「做」的动词上，其词族贯穿感情、举止与造作。

latinIntro.en: Latin facere 'to do, make' and the prefix ad- give afficere and affectio; English affection and affectionate come from that noun, with -ate and -ly as endings.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 facere「做、造」与前缀 ad- 给出 afficere 与 affectio；英语的 affection 与 affectionate 都来自这个名词，词尾为 -ate 与 -ly。

items.example: The prefix directs the action toward a person.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作指向某人。

items.example: The base verb supplies the sense of doing something to someone.
items.exampleCN: 基础动词提供「对某人做点什么」的含义。

items.meaning: to affect; to move a person
items.example: The compound verb means to produce a state in someone.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合动词意为在某人身上造成一种状态。

items.example: The noun is the direct source of English affection.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是英语 affection 的直接来源。

items.example: His affection for the town never faded.
items.exampleCN: 他对这座小镇的喜爱从未消退。

items.example: She gave her father an affectionate hug.
items.exampleCN: 她给了父亲一个深情的拥抱。

items.example: He spoke affectionately about his old school.
items.exampleCN: 他深情地谈起他的母校。

items.example: The nurses noted the old man's affectionateness.
items.exampleCN: 护士们注意到这位老人的亲切。

items.example: Her accent sounded affected.
items.exampleCN: 她的口音听起来很做作。

definition_zh: 共情；同理心；共情性理解；代入；共鸣；体谅；移情（美学）；用户体察
definition_en: the ability to understand and share the feelings of another person
core_image: 两个人隔着一张桌子，一个人说到一半停住，另一个人的手也停在杯沿上
scene: 朋友讲到一半忽然停住，对面的人没有插话，只是把杯子放下，等他把那口气缓过去。When the friend broke off mid-sentence, the other person set down the cup and waited, offering empathy rather than advice.
sceneCN: 这里 empathy 指「共情、设身处地理解并分享他人感受」（第 1 个义项）；句意为朋友讲到一半停住，对面的人放下杯子静静等候，给予的是共情而非建议。可辨识物件：桌子、两只杯子、停住的手、沉默。

pos.zh: 共情；同理心；共情性理解；代入；共鸣；体谅；移情（美学）；用户体察

derivatives.zh: 有共情力的（empathy + -etic，由名词转为性质）
共情的；移情的（empathy + -ic，更偏术语）
共情；体察（empathy + -ize，由状态转为动作）

senses.title: Feeling with another
senses.definition: the act of understanding and sharing what another person feels
senses.definitionCN: 理解并分担他人感受的行为
senses.example: She listened with empathy while he described the loss.
senses.exampleCN: 他讲述失去亲人的经过时，她带着共情倾听。
senses.why: The Greek word meant feeling inside something; the modern noun names the act of entering another person's feeling without claiming it as one's own.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊词原意为「在内部感受」；现代名词指进入他人的感受，却不把它据为己有。

senses.title: The capacity for it
senses.definition: the ability to take another's perspective and feel with them
senses.definitionCN: 采取他人视角并与之共感的能力
senses.example: Empathy can be trained, though it comes more easily to some.
senses.exampleCN: 共情能力可以训练，尽管有些人天生更容易做到。
senses.why: A single act can also be treated as a capacity, and psychology measures it as a trait.
senses.whyCN: 单次行为也可以被看作一种能力，心理学便把它当作一种特质来测量。

senses.title: The counsellor's instrument
senses.definition: in therapy, the practitioner's effort to enter the client's frame of reference
senses.definitionCN: 心理治疗中，从业者努力进入来访者的参照框架
senses.example: The counsellor's empathy helped the client put words to the fear.
senses.exampleCN: 咨询师的共情帮助来访者把那份恐惧说了出来。
senses.why: The profession turned the everyday capacity into a working tool with rules about when to speak.
senses.whyCN: 这一职业把日常能力变成一种工作工具，并规定了何时开口。

senses.title: Standing in another's place
senses.definition: the mental act of placing oneself in another's situation
senses.definitionCN: 在想象中把自己置于他人处境的行为
senses.example: Reading the diary demanded empathy with a person long dead.
senses.exampleCN: 读这本日记需要代入一个早已逝去之人的处境。
senses.why: The word covers imagination as well as feeling: one can enter a situation one has never lived.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既涵盖感受，也涵盖想象：人可以进入自己从未经历过的处境。

senses.title: Resonance with a work
senses.definition: a felt response to a story or experience that seems to match one's own
senses.definitionCN: 对故事或经历产生仿佛与自身相合的感触
senses.example: The film earns empathy rather than admiration.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影赢得的是共鸣，而非赞叹。
senses.why: Art works by placing a stranger's feeling where one's own already sits, and the noun names that placement.
senses.whyCN: 艺术把陌生人的感受放在自己感受已有的位置，这个名词正是命名这种安放。

senses.title: Consideration in daily life
senses.definition: the practical consideration shown to someone in difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 对身处困境者表现出的实际体贴
senses.example: He showed little empathy for the staff who had to reorganise their week.
senses.exampleCN: 他对那些不得不重排一周工作的员工几乎毫无体谅。
senses.why: From a feeling the word extends to its visible form: the small adjustment one makes for another.
senses.whyCN: 从感受出发，这个词延伸到其可见形式：为他人的那一点调整。

senses.title: Feeling into an object
senses.definition: in aesthetics, the projection of one's feeling into an object or scene
senses.definitionCN: 美学中把自身情感投射到对象或景物之上
senses.example: The theory of empathy holds that we feel the weight of the stone we see.
senses.exampleCN: 移情理论认为，我们会感到所见的石头的重量。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century aesthetics used the word for reading feeling into forms, a sense older than the counselling one.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪美学用这个词指把感受读进形式之中，这一义比心理咨询义更早。

senses.title: Designing from another's seat
senses.titleCN: 以他人感受为出发点的体察
senses.definition: in design and service work, the practice of understanding users' experience
senses.definitionCN: 设计与服务工作中理解使用者体验的做法
senses.example: The designer spent a day in the call centre to build empathy with customers.
senses.exampleCN: 设计师在呼叫中心待了一天，以建立对顾客的体察。
senses.why: Modern design borrowed the psychological term and made it a method rather than a mood.
senses.whyCN: 现代设计借用了这个心理学名词，把它变成方法而非心情。

intro.en: Empathy comes from Greek empatheia, built on en- 'in' and pathos 'feeling, suffering'. English took it in the early twentieth century as a rendering of German aesthetic theory. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: empathy 来自希腊 empatheia，由 en-「在内」与 pathos「感受、痛苦」构成。英语在二十世纪初借入这个词，用以转译德国的美学理论。下列年代均为约数。

items.en: Pathos meant what befalls a person and the feeling it produces. Its deeper origin is generally thought to involve a root for suffering, but that is a reconstruction rather than a proven form.
items.cn: pathos 指降临于人身上的事以及由此产生的感受。其更深来源一般被认为与表示「受苦」的词根有关，但那属重构，并非已证形式。

items.en: Empatheia meant 'feeling in', and Greek used it for strong emotion or passionate involvement. The modern psychological sense is a later narrowing.
items.cn: empatheia 意为「在内感受」，希腊语用它指强烈的情感或投入。现代心理学义是后来收窄的结果。

items.en: German aesthetic theory named the projection of feeling into forms, and English writers translated that term as empathy in the early twentieth century.
items.cn: 德国美学为「把感受投射进形式」起了专门名称，英语作者在二十世纪初把它译作 empathy。

items.en: From psychology the noun moved to counselling, then to art criticism, and recently to design and service work.
items.cn: 这个名词从心理学走向心理咨询，再到艺术批评，晚近又进入设计与服务领域。

items.en: Source uncertain (Greek root and first English date): the pre-history of pathos is a reconstruction, and the earliest English use in the modern sense is not precisely fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（希腊词根与英语首见年代）：pathos 的早期历史属重构，现代义的英语最早用例也无确切年代。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root Greek words and one look-alike with an unrelated root; group two holds words for feeling with or for others.
note.cn: 第一组是同根希腊词，另加一个词根无关的形近词；第二组是表示「与他人共感或为其动情」的词。

entries.definition: Built on syn- plus pathos: sympathy is feeling for someone's trouble, empathy is feeling with them.
entries.definitionCN: 由 syn- 加 pathos 构成：sympathy 是为他人的困境动情，empathy 是与他们一同感受。

entries.definition: A- 'without' plus pathos: the absence of feeling, the exact opposite of what empathy names.
entries.definitionCN: a-「无」加 pathos：感受的缺席，正是 empathy 所指的反面。

entries.definition: Tele- 'far' plus pathos: the claimed sensing of another's thought at a distance, not a shared feeling.
entries.definitionCN: tele-「远」加 pathos：据称能远距离感知他人想法，而不是共享感受。

entries.definition: From Old English for leisure or vacancy, with no Greek pathos at all; only the opening sound is shared.
entries.definitionCN: 来自古英语表示空闲、空无的词，与希腊 pathos 毫无关系；共同之处只在开头读音。

entries.definition: A strong feeling of pity that moves one to help; empathy may remain understanding without any action.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈的怜悯并促使人行动；empathy 可能只是理解，不含行动。

entries.definition: A grasp of another's reasons; empathy adds the felt share of their emotion.
entries.definitionCN: 对他人理由的把握；empathy 另添了对其情绪的共同感受。

entries.definition: Disposed to feel for someone's trouble; the adjective of sympathy, not of empathy.
entries.definitionCN: 倾向于为他人的困境动情；这是 sympathy 的形容词，而非 empathy 的。

entries.definition: A clear grasp of what is going on, often without any shared feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 对情况的清楚把握，常常不含共同感受。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek word for feeling, the German aesthetic origin, and the real verbs built on the noun.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊「感受」词、德国美学的来源，以及由这个名词构成的真实动词。

normal.en: En- 'in' plus pathos 'feeling': empathy is feeling inside another's feeling, not merely feeling about it.
normal.cn: en-「在内」加 pathos「感受」：共情是在他人的感受之内感受，而不只是对其有所感。

normal.en: The same pathos root runs through sympathy, apathy and telepathy, and the prefix tells them apart.
normal.cn: 同一个 pathos 词根贯穿 sympathy、apathy 与 telepathy，靠前缀区分。

normal.en: Empathize is the verb, empathetic and empathic the adjectives, and empathizer the person.
normal.cn: 动词是 empathize，形容词是 empathetic 与 empathic，指人的名词是 empathizer。

normal.en: Counselling uses the noun for a professional skill, which is why it appears with show and lack.
normal.cn: 心理咨询把这个名词当作专业技能，因此常与「表现」和「缺乏」连用。

normal.en: Design work turned it into a method: spend time where the user sits.
normal.cn: 设计工作把它变成一种方法：到使用者所在的位置待上一段时间。

abstract.en: Picture two cups on a table and one hand that stops before lifting.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上两只杯子，以及一只在举起之前停住的手。

abstract.en: Picture a diary left open at a page written by someone you never met.
abstract.cn: 想象一本摊开的日记，那一页出自你从未见过的人之手。

abstract.en: Picture a stone in a gallery that viewers say feels heavy in the chest.
abstract.cn: 想象画廊里一块石头，观者说看着它胸口会发沉。

examples.en: Good doctors combine technical skill with empathy.
examples.cn: 好医生把技术能力与共情结合起来。

examples.en: His empathy for the displaced families shaped the policy.
examples.cn: 他对流离失所家庭的体谅影响了这项政策。

examples.en: The novel asks for empathy with a character who does terrible things.
examples.cn: 这部小说要求读者共情一个做出可怕之事的角色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「em（在内）+ pathy（感受）」——走进别人的感受里 → 共情、同理心

root: 希腊 empatheia = en-（在内）+ pathos（感受、痛苦）；由「在内部感受」引申为「共情、同理」。pathos 更深词根属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one pause at a table: feeling with another, the capacity behind it, the counsellor's tool, standing in another's place, resonance with a story, everyday consideration, feeling projected into an object, and design that begins from the user's seat.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕桌边的一次停顿展开：与他人一同感受、背后的能力、咨询师的工具、代入他人处境、与故事的共鸣、日常的体谅、投射到对象上的感受，以及从使用者位置出发的设计。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people at a table, one hand stopping at the rim of a cup.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌边的两个人，一只手停在杯沿上。

branches.en: THE ACT AND THE CAPACITY: feeling with someone, and the ability that makes it possible.
branches.cn: 行为与能力：与他人一同感受，以及使这件事成为可能的能力。

branches.en: THE PROFESSIONAL TOOL: the counsellor's trained entry into a client's frame of reference.
branches.cn: 专业工具：咨询师受训后进入来访者参照框架的做法。

branches.en: ENTERING ANOTHER'S WORLD: standing in a situation one never lived, and resonating with a story.
branches.cn: 进入他人的世界：代入从未经历过的处境，以及与故事产生共鸣。

branches.en: EMPATHY IN PRACTICE: everyday consideration, and design that starts from the user's seat.
branches.cn: 实践中的共情：日常的体谅，以及从使用者位置出发的设计。

branches.en: FEELING INTO FORM: the aesthetic sense in which a stone can feel heavy.
branches.cn: 感受进入形式：美学义，在那里的石头可以显得沉重。

intro.en: Empathy is built from Greek pieces, and its family covers the noun, two adjectives, the verb and the person.
intro.cn: empathy 由希腊语构件构成，其词族包括名词、两个形容词、动词与指人的名词。

latinIntro.en: These are Greek, not Latin, elements: en- 'in', pathos 'feeling', and the noun ending -eia. No Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 这些是希腊语而非拉丁语构件：en-「在内」、pathos「感受」以及名词词尾 -eia。因此不列拉丁词条。

items.example: The prefix places the feeling inside the other person.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把感受放进他人之内。

items.example: The root supplies the emotional core of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供这个词的情感核心。

items.example: The Greek noun is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊名词是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: She listened with empathy while he described the loss.
items.exampleCN: 他讲述失去亲人的经过时，她带着共情倾听。

items.example: The therapist kept an empathic distance.
items.exampleCN: 治疗师保持着共情的距离。

items.example: Her reply was brief and empathetic.
items.exampleCN: 她的回答简短而体察人心。

items.example: He found it hard to empathize with the manager.
items.exampleCN: 他发现很难对那位经理共情。

items.example: She is a natural empathizer.
items.exampleCN: 她天生善解人意。

items.example: He responded empathetically rather than defensively.
items.exampleCN: 他以共情而非防卫的方式回应。

definition_zh: 有共情力的；体察他人处境的；善解人意的；同理式的；移情的；令人代入的；体谅的；以用户感受为中心的
definition_en: able to understand and share what another person is feeling
core_image: 一个人听人说话时，眉毛先于对方皱了起来
scene: 会议里有人低声说家里出了事，坐在斜对面的同事没有追问，只把会议记录推到一边。When a colleague mentioned a family emergency in a low voice, the woman across the table said nothing and quietly moved the minutes aside, an empathetic response.
sceneCN: 这里 empathetic 指「体察他人处境的回应」（第 2 个义项：以举动体现对他人感受的理解）；句意为同事低声提到家中急事，斜对面的女士没有追问，只把会议记录推到一边，这便是体察他人处境的回应。可辨识物件：会议桌、记录本、推开的动作、压低的声音。

pos.zh: 有共情力的；体察他人处境的；善解人意的；同理式的；移情的；令人代入的；体谅的；以用户感受为中心的

collocations.zh: 以用户感受为中心的设计

derivatives.zh: 共情；同理心（empathetic 的基础名词）
共情地（empathetic 的副词变体）
共情；体察（empathy + -ize，由性质转为动作）

senses.title: A person who feels with others
senses.definition: of a person, readily understanding and sharing the feelings of others
senses.definitionCN: 指人容易理解并分担他人的感受
senses.example: She is the most empathetic person in the department.
senses.exampleCN: 她是部门里最有共情力的人。
senses.why: The adjective moves the noun onto a person: empathy is the capacity, and empathetic says that someone has it.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把名词移到人身上：empathy 是能力，empathetic 则说明某人拥有这种能力。

senses.title: A reply that fits the feeling
senses.titleCN: 与对方感受相称的回应
senses.definition: of a response or action, showing that another's feeling has been understood
senses.definitionCN: 指回应或举动显示已理解对方的感受
senses.example: His empathetic reply was to sit down and say nothing for a moment.
senses.exampleCN: 他的回应是坐下来，先沉默片刻，这正体察了对方的感受。
senses.why: A response can demonstrate understanding even when no words are offered, which is why the adjective often describes actions.
senses.whyCN: 即使没有言语，回应也能显示理解，因此这个形容词常用来描述动作。

senses.title: A temperament that notices
senses.definition: having a temperament that notices and cares about others' states
senses.definitionCN: 具有留意并关心他人状态的性格
senses.example: The nurses described him as empathetic and unhurried.
senses.exampleCN: 护士们说他善解人意，而且从不急躁。
senses.why: Temperament is the standing version of a single act: what someone does once, an empathetic person does by habit.
senses.whyCN: 性格是单次行为的持久版本：某人偶一为之的事，善解人意者会习惯性地去做。

senses.title: Listening that gives room
senses.definition: of a way of listening that leaves the speaker room to finish
senses.definitionCN: 指一种让说话者把话说完的倾听方式
senses.example: Her empathetic listening kept him talking when he might have stopped.
senses.exampleCN: 她共情式的倾听让他在本可能停下时继续说了下去。
senses.why: The word can describe technique as well as feeling, because listening has a form that can be learned.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既可描述感受，也可描述技巧，因为倾听有一种可以学会的形式。

senses.title: The clinical sense
senses.definition: in psychology, relating to the practitioner's entry into another's experience
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中，指从业者进入他人体验的做法
senses.example: The training stresses an empathetic stance rather than quick interpretation.
senses.exampleCN: 培训强调共情的立场，而非急于作出解释。
senses.why: Clinical writing needed an adjective for the trained stance, and chose this one over the older variant.
senses.whyCN: 临床写作需要一个形容词来指受训后的立场，于是选用了这个较新的变体。

senses.title: Work that holds the viewer
senses.definition: of a story or image, drawing the audience into a character's feeling
senses.definitionCN: 指故事或影像把观众带入角色的感受
senses.example: The documentary is empathetic without ever becoming sentimental.
senses.exampleCN: 这部纪录片让人代入，却从不流于感伤。
senses.why: Art can lend feeling without claiming it, and criticism uses the adjective for that loan.
senses.whyCN: 艺术可以借出感受而不将其据为己有，评论便用这个形容词指这种出借。

senses.title: Considerate under pressure
senses.definition: showing consideration for someone in a difficult position
senses.definitionCN: 对处境困难者表现出体贴
senses.example: The manager was empathetic about the deadline and moved it by a week.
senses.exampleCN: 经理对截止期限的处理很体谅，把它往后挪了一周。
senses.why: Consideration becomes visible when a rule is bent for a person, and the adjective covers that small bend.
senses.whyCN: 当规则为某个人稍作弯折时，体谅就变得可见，这个形容词正涵盖那一点弯折。

senses.title: Designed from the user's seat
senses.titleCN: 从使用者位置出发的设计
senses.definition: in design and service work, based on an understanding of users' experience
senses.definitionCN: 设计与服务工作中，建立在理解使用者体验之上
senses.example: The team ran an empathetic review of the complaint logs.
senses.exampleCN: 团队对投诉记录做了一次以用户感受为中心的复核。
senses.why: Design borrowed the word and made it a method: read the logs, sit in the chair, then build.
senses.whyCN: 设计借用了这个词并把它变成方法：读记录、坐进那把椅子，然后再动手。

intro.en: Empathetic is empathy plus the Greek adjective ending -etikos, and it competes with the older empathic. Empathy itself comes from Greek empatheia, from en- 'in' and pathos 'feeling'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: empathetic 是 empathy 加希腊形容词词尾 -etikos 构成，与更早的 empathic 并存。empathy 本身来自希腊 empatheia，由 en-「在内」与 pathos「感受」构成。下列年代均为约数。

items.en: Pathos meant what a person undergoes and the feeling it produces. Its deeper origin is generally thought to involve a root for suffering, but the form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: pathos 指人所经历的事以及由此产生的感受。其更深来源一般被认为与表示「受苦」的词根有关，但该形式属重构。

items.en: The noun entered English in the early twentieth century as a rendering of German aesthetic theory, then moved into psychology.
items.cn: 这个名词在二十世纪初进入英语，用以转译德国美学理论，随后进入心理学。

items.en: Empathic follows the shorter Greek pattern; empathetic follows the longer one and became common in clinical and general prose. Neither is wrong, and style guides differ.
items.cn: empathic 依循较短的希腊构词模式；empathetic 依循较长的模式，在临床与一般文章中更为常见。两者都不算错，各家体例偏好不同。

items.en: From counselling the adjective spread to management writing, art criticism and design, often before the response rather than the person.
items.cn: 这个形容词从心理咨询扩散到管理写作、艺术批评与设计，常放在「回应」之前而非「人」之前。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root and first date): the pre-history of pathos is a reconstruction, and the first English use of this adjective is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根与首见年代）：pathos 的早期历史属重构，这个形容词的英语最早用例也无确切年代。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root forms and two adjectives that look close but mean something else; group two holds words for understanding others' feelings.
note.cn: 第一组是同根形式，另加两个形近却另有含义的形容词；第二组是表示理解他人感受的词。

entries.definition: The capacity itself; empathetic describes a person or response that shows it.
entries.definitionCN: 指能力本身；empathetic 形容表现这种能力的人或回应。

entries.definition: The older and shorter adjective, common in clinical writing; the meaning is the same as empathetic.
entries.definitionCN: 更早、更短的形容词，常见于临床写作；含义与 empathetic 相同。

entries.definition: From Greek emphasis 'display', meaning forcefully stressed; it has no pathos and no feeling in its root.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 emphasis「显示」，意为强调的；词根里既无 pathos，也无感受。

entries.definition: Built on pathos but means sadly inadequate or deserving pity; the prefix, not the root, separates it.
entries.definitionCN: 建在 pathos 上，却意为可怜、差劲；区分它的是前缀而非词根。

entries.definition: Feeling sorry for someone's trouble; empathetic implies sharing the feeling itself.
entries.definitionCN: 为他人的困境感到难过；empathetic 意味着共享那份感受本身。

entries.definition: Pity joined to a readiness to help; empathetic may stay with understanding.
entries.definitionCN: 怜悯并伴随帮助的意愿；empathetic 可能只停留在理解。

entries.definition: Able to see why someone acts as they do; empathetic adds the felt side.
entries.definitionCN: 能看出某人为何如此行事；empathetic 另添了感受的一面。

entries.definition: Quick to notice others' states, sometimes to one's own cost; empathetic stresses the sharing, not the noticing.
entries.definitionCN: 容易察觉他人状态，有时以自身为代价；empathetic 强调共享，而非察觉。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek root of feeling, the two real adjective forms, and the real settings where the word is used.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊「感受」词根、两个真实的形容词形式，以及这个词真实出现的场合。

normal.en: Empathy plus -etic gives the adjective, just as energy plus -etic gives energetic.
normal.cn: empathy 加 -etic 构成形容词，正如 energy 加 -etic 构成 energetic。

normal.en: Emphatic looks like this word but means forcefully stressed, so the two must be kept apart by their roots.
normal.cn: emphatic 字形相近却意为强调的，两者必须靠词根分清。

normal.en: The older empathic survives in clinical writing; empathetic is the common general form.
normal.cn: 较旧的 empathic 仍用于临床写作；empathetic 是常见的一般形式。

normal.en: It often sits before response, listening, approach and leader.
normal.cn: 它常放在回应、倾听、做法与领导者之前。

normal.en: The adverb empathetically marks how something is done, not what is felt.
normal.cn: 副词 empathetically 标示做事的方式，而非感受的内容。

abstract.en: Picture a brow that folds a moment before the speaker's does.
abstract.cn: 想象一道眉毛比说话者更早皱起。

abstract.en: Picture a notebook pushed aside without a word, because the note can wait.
abstract.cn: 想象一本记录本被无声地推到一边，因为记录可以等。

abstract.en: Picture a chair in a call centre occupied by a designer for one full shift.
abstract.cn: 想象一名设计师在呼叫中心的椅子上坐满一整班。

examples.en: An empathetic teacher notices the student who has stopped asking questions.
examples.cn: 有共情力的老师会注意到那个不再提问的学生。

examples.en: The report recommends a more empathetic approach to complaints.
examples.cn: 报告建议以更体察对方的方式处理投诉。

examples.en: Her empathetic silence gave him time to finish.
examples.cn: 她体谅的沉默给了他时间把话说完。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「em（在内）+ pathetic（感受的）」——能走进别人感受里的 → 有共情力的

root: 希腊 empatheia（en-「在内」+ pathos「感受」）+ 形容词词尾 -etikos；与更早的 empathic 同义并存。pathos 更深词根属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one early frown: a person who feels with others, a reply that fits the feeling, a noticing temperament, listening that leaves room, a clinical stance, a work that holds the viewer, consideration under pressure, and design from the user's seat.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一次提前皱起的眉展开：与他人同感的人、与感受相称的回应、善于察觉的性格、留出空间的倾听、临床立场、令人代入的作品、困境中的体谅，以及从使用者位置出发的设计。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a brow that folds a moment before the speaker's brow does.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道比说话者更早皱起的眉毛。

branches.en: THE PERSON AND THE TRAIT: someone who feels with others, and the temperament that makes it habitual.
branches.cn: 人与性格：与他人同感的人，以及使这件事成为习惯的性格。

branches.en: THE RESPONSE AND THE BEND: a reply that fits the feeling, and a rule moved for a person under pressure.
branches.cn: 回应与弯折：与感受相称的回应，以及为困境中的人挪动的规则。

branches.en: THE FORM OF LISTENING: silence that leaves the speaker room to finish.
branches.cn: 倾听的形式：让说话者把话说完的沉默。

branches.en: TRAINED AND BORROWED: the clinical stance, and the story that lends feeling to a viewer.
branches.cn: 受训与借出：临床立场，以及把感受借给观众的故事。

branches.en: DESIGNED FROM ANOTHER'S SEAT: a method that begins with the user's experience.
branches.cn: 从他人位置出发的设计：以使用者体验为起点的方法。

intro.en: Empathetic is the longer of two adjectives built on empathy, which is itself built from Greek pieces.
intro.cn: empathetic 是建在 empathy 之上的两个形容词中较长的那个，而 empathy 本身由希腊语构件构成。

latinIntro.en: The parts are Greek, not Latin: en- 'in', pathos 'feeling', and the adjective ending -etikos. No Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 这些构件属希腊语而非拉丁语：en-「在内」、pathos「感受」，以及形容词词尾 -etikos。因此不列拉丁词条。
