definition_zh: 同情；同情心；慰问；赞同；共鸣；体恤；相互感应；引人同情的感染力
definition_en: a feeling of pity or support for someone in trouble
core_image: 灵堂外的一张木桌，上面放着一束用麻绳捆好的白花
scene: 灵堂外的走廊上，邻居把一束白花放在桌上，只说了一句节哀，便退到门边。In the corridor outside the chapel a neighbour laid a bunch of white flowers on the table, offered a few words of sympathy, and stepped back to the door.
sceneCN: 这里 sympathy 指「慰问、哀悼之意」（第 3 个义项：对丧家表达慰问的话）；句意为邻居把白花放在桌上，说了一句节哀便退到门边。可辨识物件：走廊、木桌、白花、麻绳、门边。

pos.zh: 同情；同情心；慰问；赞同；共鸣；体恤；相互感应；引人同情的感染力

derivatives.zh: 同情的；赞同的（sympathy + -etic，由名词转为性质）
同情；赞同（sympathy + -ize，由感受转为动作）

senses.title: Sorrow for another's trouble
senses.definition: a feeling of pity and sorrow for someone who suffers
senses.definitionCN: 对遭受不幸者感到怜悯与难过
senses.example: She felt sympathy for the family who lost their home.
senses.exampleCN: 她为失去家园的那家人感到难过。
senses.why: The Greek word meant feeling with someone; English narrowed it toward feeling for someone in distress.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊词原意为「与他人一同感受」；英语把它收窄为对身处困境者的感受。

senses.title: The quality of feeling it
senses.definition: the disposition to feel pity for others
senses.definitionCN: 易于对他人生出怜悯的性格
senses.example: He has little sympathy for people who complain without acting.
senses.exampleCN: 他对只抱怨而不行动的人没什么同情心。
senses.why: A single feeling becomes a trait when it is spoken of as something a person has or lacks.
senses.whyCN: 当一种感受被说成某人拥有或缺乏的东西时，它就成了性格特质。

senses.title: Words sent to the bereaved
senses.definition: an expression of condolence, spoken or written
senses.definitionCN: 口头或书面的哀悼与慰问
senses.example: We sent a letter of sympathy to the widow.
senses.exampleCN: 我们给遗孀寄了一封慰问信。
senses.why: Mourning needed a conventional form, and the noun came to name the words themselves.
senses.whyCN: 丧礼需要一种惯用的形式，这个名词于是用来指那些话本身。

senses.title: Agreement with a cause
senses.definition: support for an opinion, movement or proposal
senses.definitionCN: 对某种意见、运动或提案的支持
senses.example: The proposal won sympathy from both sides of the chamber.
senses.exampleCN: 这项提案赢得了议会两方的赞同。
senses.why: Feeling with a person extends to feeling with an idea, and the word covers political agreement.
senses.whyCN: 与人同感会扩展到与某种想法同感，这个词因而涵盖政治上的赞同。

senses.title: Two things in tune
senses.definition: a natural harmony of feeling between people
senses.definitionCN: 人与人之间感受上的自然和谐
senses.example: There is a sympathy between their two voices that makes singing together easy.
senses.exampleCN: 他们两人的嗓音之间有一种共鸣，使合唱变得轻松。
senses.why: Before it named pity, the word named likeness: things that answer each other were said to be in sympathy.
senses.whyCN: 在指怜悯之前，这个词先指相似：彼此呼应的事物被说成处于相互感应之中。

senses.title: Understanding a hard position
senses.definition: consideration shown for someone's difficult circumstances
senses.definitionCN: 对某人艰难处境的体谅
senses.example: The warden showed sympathy for the prisoners' conditions.
senses.exampleCN: 监狱长对囚犯的处境表示了体恤。
senses.why: Pity that stays general is cheap; the word is also used for the specific allowance made to a person.
senses.whyCN: 泛泛的怜悯并不值钱；这个词也用于对某个人作出的具体通融。

senses.title: Iron and the magnet
senses.definition: in older science, an attraction or mutual influence between bodies
senses.definitionCN: 旧时科学中物体之间的吸引或相互影响
senses.example: The old physics text speaks of a sympathy between iron and the magnet.
senses.exampleCN: 那本旧物理书谈到铁与磁石之间的相互感应。
senses.why: Natural philosophy used the word for hidden affinities before it was applied to human feeling.
senses.whyCN: 自然哲学先用这个词指隐秘的亲和力，后来才用于人的情感。

senses.title: The pull of a flawed hero
senses.definition: the power of a story or character to draw out pity
senses.definitionCN: 故事或人物激起怜悯的力量
senses.example: The play depends on the sympathy it builds for a flawed hero.
senses.exampleCN: 这部剧依靠它对一个有缺陷的英雄所积累起的同情。
senses.why: Critics borrowed the noun for the feeling an audience is led into, which is a craft and not a mood.
senses.whyCN: 评论家借用这个名词指观众被引导进入的感受，那是一种技艺，而非心情。

intro.en: Sympathy comes from Greek sympatheia, built on syn- 'with' and pathos 'feeling'. English took it in the sixteenth century, first for natural affinities and later for pity. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: sympathy 来自希腊 sympatheia，由 syn-「同、与」与 pathos「感受」构成。英语在十六世纪借入，先指事物间的自然亲和，后指怜悯。下列年代均为约数。

items.en: Pathos meant what one undergoes and the feeling it brings. Its deeper origin is generally thought to involve a root for suffering, but that is a reconstruction.
items.cn: pathos 指人所经历的事以及它带来的感受。其更深来源一般被认为与表示「受苦」的词根有关，但那属重构。

items.en: Sympatheia meant a shared experience or mutual feeling, and Greek also used it for the affinity between parts of the natural world.
items.cn: sympatheia 指共同的经历或相互的感受，希腊语也用它指自然界各部分之间的亲和。

items.en: English used the word from the sixteenth century for hidden attractions between bodies, a sense now confined to histories of science.
items.cn: 英语从十六世纪起用这个词指物体之间隐秘的吸引，这一义今天只留在科学史中。

items.en: The emotional sense widened in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, and the condolence sense followed from it.
items.cn: 情感义在十七、十八世纪扩展，慰问义又由它而来。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root and first date): the pre-history of pathos is a reconstruction, and the shift from natural affinity to pity is inferred from usage rather than documented in one step.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根与首见年代）：pathos 的早期历史属重构；从自然亲和到怜悯的转变是从用法推断的，并非一步到位的文献记录。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root words and one look-alike from a different Greek root; group two holds words for pity and for sharing feeling.
note.cn: 第一组是同根词，另加一个来自不同希腊词根的形近词；第二组是表示怜悯与共享感受的词。

entries.definition: The adjective for feeling or showing sympathy; it describes the person or response, not the feeling itself.
entries.definitionCN: 表示抱有或表现出同情的形容词；它描述人或回应，而非感受本身。

entries.definition: To feel or express sympathy; the verb turns the noun into an act.
entries.definitionCN: 感到或表达同情；这个动词把名词变成动作。

entries.definition: En- 'in' plus pathos: empathy shares the feeling, while sympathy feels for the sufferer.
entries.definitionCN: en-「在内」加 pathos：empathy 共享感受，而 sympathy 是为受苦者感到难过。

entries.definition: Syn- plus phone 'sound': a sounding together of notes, with no pathos in its root despite the look.
entries.definitionCN: syn- 加 phone「声音」：音符同响，尽管字形相似，词根里并无 pathos。

entries.definition: Pity that moves a person to help; sympathy can remain a feeling with no act.
entries.definitionCN: 促使人伸出援手的怜悯；sympathy 可能只是感受而无行动。

entries.definition: Sorrow for another's suffering, often with a hint of condescension; sympathy is more respectful.
entries.definitionCN: 对他人苦难的难过，常带一丝居高临下；sympathy 更显尊重。

entries.definition: The formal expression of grief to the bereaved; sympathy is the feeling behind it and can also name the words.
entries.definitionCN: 向丧家正式表达的哀悼；sympathy 是其背后的感受，也可指那些话。

entries.definition: Understanding another's emotion from inside; sympathy looks at the sufferer from alongside.
entries.definitionCN: 从内部理解他人的情绪；sympathy 则是从旁看着受苦者。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek prefix and root, the real condolence phrases, and the real derived words.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊前缀与词根、真实的慰问搭配，以及真实的派生词。

normal.en: Syn- 'with' plus pathos 'feeling': sympathy is feeling alongside someone, while empathy is feeling inside them.
normal.cn: syn-「与」加 pathos「感受」：sympathy 是在某人身边感受，而 empathy 是在其内部感受。

normal.en: The same root runs through apathy, telepathy and pathetic, and each prefix or ending shifts the meaning.
normal.cn: 同一个词根贯穿 apathy、telepathy 与 pathetic，前缀或词尾各自改变含义。

normal.en: Phrases to keep: express sympathy, a letter of sympathy, have sympathy for.
normal.cn: 应记住的搭配：表达慰问、慰问信、对……抱有同情。

normal.en: The older sense survives in the history of science, where iron and the magnet are in sympathy.
normal.cn: 较旧的义项留在科学史里：铁与磁石处于相互感应之中。

normal.en: The plural sympathies often means condolences, as in my sympathies.
normal.cn: 复数 sympathies 常指慰问之意，如「谨致慰问」。

abstract.en: Picture white flowers tied with twine on a table outside a door.
abstract.cn: 想象门外桌上用麻绳捆好的白花。

abstract.en: Picture two voices that fall into the same rhythm without rehearsal.
abstract.cn: 想象两个嗓音未经排练便落入同一节奏。

abstract.en: Picture a magnet under a sheet of paper, moving iron filings without touching them.
abstract.cn: 想象纸下的一块磁石，不接触却让铁屑移动。

examples.en: She has deep sympathy for families who arrive with nothing.
examples.cn: 她对一无所有而来的家庭怀有深切的同情。

examples.en: The union expressed sympathy with the strikers' demand.
examples.cn: 工会对罢工者的诉求表示赞同。

examples.en: Please accept my sympathy at this difficult time.
examples.cn: 在这个艰难时刻，请接受我的慰问。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「sym（相同）+ pathy（感受）」——与他人有相同的感受 → 同情、共鸣

root: 希腊 sympatheia = syn-（同、与）+ pathos（感受）；先指事物间相互感应，后收窄为「同情、慰问」。pathos 更深词根属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one bunch of white flowers: sorrow for another, the disposition behind it, the words sent to the bereaved, agreement with a cause, a natural harmony between people, consideration for a hard position, an old attraction between bodies, and the pity a story draws out.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一束白花展开：为他人的难过、其背后的性格、送给丧家的话、对某种主张的赞同、人与人之间自然的和谐、对困境的体恤、旧时物与物之间的吸引，以及故事所唤起的怜悯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: white flowers tied with twine on a table outside a door.
core.cn: 核心意象：门外桌上用麻绳捆好的白花。

branches.en: THE FEELING AND THE QUALITY: sorrow for someone in trouble, and the disposition to feel it.
branches.cn: 感受与品质：为困境中的人难过，以及易于生出这种难过的性格。

branches.en: THE WORDS SENT: condolence that turns a feeling into a conventional form.
branches.cn: 送出的话：把感受变成惯用形式的慰问。

branches.en: AGREEING AND RESONATING: support for a cause, and a natural harmony between two people.
branches.cn: 赞同与呼应：对某种主张的支持，以及两人之间自然的和谐。

branches.en: THE SPECIFIC ALLOWANCE: consideration shown for one person's hard circumstances.
branches.cn: 具体的通融：对某个人艰难处境的体谅。

branches.en: OLD SCIENCE AND NEW ART: hidden attraction between bodies, and the pity a story draws out.
branches.cn: 旧科学与新艺术：物体之间隐秘的吸引，以及故事所唤起的怜悯。

intro.en: Sympathy is Greek in its pieces, and its family covers the noun, the adjective, the verb and the person.
intro.cn: sympathy 的构件属希腊语，其词族包括名词、形容词、动词与指人的名词。

latinIntro.en: Syn- 'with', pathos 'feeling' and -eia build the noun; -etic, -ize and -er build the rest. These are Greek elements, so no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: syn-「与」、pathos「感受」与 -eia 构成名词；-etic、-ize 与 -er 构成其余形式。这些是希腊语构件，因此不列拉丁词条。

items.example: The prefix places the feeling alongside another person.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把感受放在他人身旁。

items.example: The root supplies the emotional core.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供情感核心。

items.example: The Greek noun stands behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊名词是整个词族的来源。

items.example: She felt sympathy for the family who lost their home.
items.exampleCN: 她为失去家园的那家人感到难过。

items.example: The letter was short and sympathetic.
items.exampleCN: 那封信简短而充满同情。

items.example: He sympathized with the workers' demand.
items.exampleCN: 他赞同工人们的诉求。

items.example: The movement had many sympathizers abroad.
items.exampleCN: 这场运动在国外有许多同情者。

items.example: She listened sympathetically.
items.exampleCN: 她同情地听着。

items.example: My sympathies go to the family.
items.exampleCN: 谨向这家人致以慰问。

definition_zh: 同情的；表示慰问的；赞同的；体谅的；讨人喜欢的；交感神经的；相互呼应的；令人同情的
definition_en: showing that one understands and feels for another's trouble
core_image: 候诊室里，一把椅子被悄悄往前挪了半臂的距离
scene: 候诊室里，一个男人描述疼痛时声音发抖，护士没有打断，只把椅子往前挪了挪。In the waiting room the nurse moved her chair closer and let the man finish describing the pain before she spoke, a sympathetic listener.
sceneCN: 这里 sympathetic 指「同情的」（第 1 个义项：对他人的痛苦表示理解与难过）；句意为男人描述疼痛时声音发抖，护士没有打断，只把椅子往前挪近。可辨识物件：候诊椅、病历夹、发抖的手、挪动的距离。

pos.zh: 同情的；表示慰问的；赞同的；体谅的；讨人喜欢的；交感神经的；相互呼应的；令人同情的

derivatives.zh: 同情；共鸣（sympathetic 的基础名词）
不同情的；冷漠的（un- + sympathetic，语义反向）
同情；赞同（sympathy + -ize，由性质转为动作）

senses.title: Feeling for someone's pain
senses.titleCN: 对他人的痛苦感到难过
senses.definition: showing that one feels for another person's suffering
senses.definitionCN: 表现出对他人苦难的体恤与难过
senses.example: The nurse was sympathetic when he described the pain.
senses.exampleCN: 他描述疼痛时，护士表现出同情。
senses.why: The adjective puts the noun's feeling into a person's face or manner, where it can be seen.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把名词所指的感受放到人的神情与举止上，使其可见。

senses.title: Words for the bereaved
senses.definition: expressing condolence in words or writing
senses.definitionCN: 以口头或书面方式表达哀悼
senses.example: He sent a sympathetic note to the family.
senses.exampleCN: 他给那家人寄去一封慰问短笺。
senses.why: Condolence needs a conventional form, and the adjective marks the tone of the form rather than the feeling behind it.
senses.whyCN: 慰问需要惯用的形式，这个形容词标示的是形式的语气，而非其背后的感受。

senses.title: On the side of a cause
senses.definition: favourable to a proposal, movement or demand
senses.definitionCN: 对提案、运动或诉求持赞成态度
senses.example: The newspaper was sympathetic to the strike.
senses.exampleCN: 那家报纸对这次罢工持同情态度。
senses.why: Feeling for people extends to feeling for what they ask, and the adjective follows the demand.
senses.whyCN: 对人的体恤会延伸到对他们所求之事的体恤，这个形容词便跟着诉求走。

senses.title: A view that allows for difficulty
senses.definition: willing to take someone's difficult circumstances into account
senses.definitionCN: 愿意把某人的艰难处境纳入考量
senses.example: The court took a sympathetic view of her circumstances.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭对她的处境采取了体谅的看法。
senses.why: Sympathy that stays a feeling changes nothing; this sense marks the moment it changes a judgment.
senses.whyCN: 只停留在感受上的同情不改变任何事；这一义项标示它改变判断的那一刻。

senses.title: Easy to like
senses.definition: pleasant and likeable in manner or character
senses.definitionCN: 举止或性格令人愉快、让人喜欢
senses.example: The new neighbour turned out to be a sympathetic man.
senses.exampleCN: 新来的邻居原来是个讨人喜欢的人。
senses.why: A person who answers your feeling is pleasant to be near, and the adjective slid from pity to likability.
senses.whyCN: 能回应你感受的人相处起来愉快，这个形容词便从怜悯滑向讨人喜欢。

senses.title: The nerve that answers
senses.definition: in anatomy, relating to the system of nerves that responds to stress
senses.definitionCN: 解剖学上，指对应激作出反应的那套神经
senses.example: The sympathetic nervous system controls the body's quick responses.
senses.exampleCN: 交感神经系统控制身体的快速反应。
senses.why: Old physiology saw organs responding together as a kind of sympathy, and the anatomical name kept that image.
senses.whyCN: 旧时的生理学把器官的协同反应看作一种「共感」，解剖学名称保留了这一意象。

senses.title: Answering another thing
senses.definition: naturally responsive to or in tune with something else
senses.definitionCN: 与另一事物自然相应、彼此合拍
senses.example: The two poems are sympathetic in tone, as if written in answer to each other.
senses.exampleCN: 两首诗在语调上彼此呼应，仿佛互相作答。
senses.why: The oldest layer of the root is affinity between things, and this sense keeps it alive outside medicine.
senses.whyCN: 这个词根最古老的一层是事物之间的亲和，这一义项让它在医学之外仍然存活。

senses.title: The character we pity
senses.definition: in a story, drawn so that the audience feels for them
senses.definitionCN: 在故事中被写得让观众为其动情
senses.example: The novel's most sympathetic character is also its most foolish.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说里最令人同情的角色也是最愚蠢的那个。
senses.why: Writers treat sympathy as a craft: the audience is led to feel, and the adjective describes the result.
senses.whyCN: 写作者把同情当作一种技艺：观众被引导去感受，这个形容词描述其结果。

intro.en: Sympathetic is sympathy plus the Greek adjective ending -etikos. Sympathy comes from Greek sympatheia, syn- 'with' and pathos 'feeling'. The anatomical sense arose from older physiology. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: sympathetic 是 sympathy 加希腊形容词词尾 -etikos 构成。sympathy 来自希腊 sympatheia，由 syn-「同、与」与 pathos「感受」构成。解剖学义来自更早的生理学观念。下列年代均为约数。

items.en: Pathos meant what one undergoes and the feeling it brings. Its deeper origin is generally thought to involve a root for suffering, but that is a reconstruction rather than a proven form.
items.cn: pathos 指人所经历的事以及它带来的感受。其更深来源一般被认为与表示「受苦」的词根有关，但那属重构，并非已证形式。

items.en: Sympatheia named shared experience and mutual influence, including the affinity between parts of nature. The adjective was formed within Greek from the same pieces.
items.cn: sympatheia 指共同的经历与相互影响，包括自然界各部分之间的亲和。其形容词也在希腊语内部由同一批构件构成。

items.en: English used the adjective from the sixteenth century for things acting on one another, and for persons disposed to feel for others.
items.cn: 英语从十六世纪起用这个形容词指事物之间的相互作用，也指乐于为他人动情的人。

items.en: Older physiology described organs responding together as a sympathy, and the name sympathetic nerves kept that image in anatomy.
items.cn: 更早的生理学把器官的协同反应称作一种「共感」，交感神经的名称把这个意象留在了解剖学中。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root and first date): the pre-history of pathos is a reconstruction, and the first English use of the adjective is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根与首见年代）：pathos 的早期历史属重构，这个形容词的英语最早用例也无确切年代。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root forms and one look-alike from a different Greek root; group two holds words for being kind to someone in trouble.
note.cn: 第一组是同根形式，另加一个来自不同希腊词根的形近词；第二组是表示善待困境中人的词。

entries.definition: The feeling itself; sympathetic describes the person, words or view that carry it.
entries.definitionCN: 指感受本身；sympathetic 形容承载它的那种人、话语或看法。

entries.definition: To feel or express sympathy; the verb names the act, the adjective the manner.
entries.definitionCN: 感到或表达同情；动词命名行为，形容词命名方式。

entries.definition: Built on en- plus pathos: it shares the feeling from inside, while sympathetic looks on with pity.
entries.definitionCN: 由 en- 加 pathos 构成：它从内部共享感受，而 sympathetic 是从旁怜悯。

entries.definition: From Greek symptoma 'a chance happening', the source of symptom; it means indicative of a condition, not kind.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 symptoma「偶然发生之事」，即 symptom 的来源；意为「表明某种病况的」，与善意无关。

entries.definition: Pity that leads to action; sympathetic may remain a manner or a view.
entries.definitionCN: 导向行动的怜悯；sympathetic 可能只停留在态度或看法。

entries.definition: Actively encouraging and helping; sympathetic offers understanding and may offer nothing more.
entries.definitionCN: 积极鼓励并给予帮助；sympathetic 提供理解，可能别无其他。

entries.definition: Able to see why someone acted as they did; sympathetic adds the feeling for their trouble.
entries.definitionCN: 能看出某人为何如此行事；sympathetic 另添了对其困境的难过。

entries.definition: Pleasant and easy to like; sympathetic in its fifth sense means much the same, but by way of pity.
entries.definitionCN: 令人愉快、容易让人喜欢；sympathetic 的第五义与此相近，但经由怜悯而来。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek root, the real anatomical phrase, and the real derived words of the noun.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊词根、真实的解剖学搭配，以及名词真实的派生词。

normal.en: Sym- 'with' plus pathos 'feeling': the sympathetic person feels alongside, and the sympathetic nerve answers alongside other organs.
normal.cn: sym-「与」加 pathos「感受」：有同情心的人是在旁一同感受，交感神经也是与其他器官一同应答。

normal.en: The adjective is used of listeners, responses, views and characters, which shows how far it has travelled from pure pity.
normal.cn: 这个形容词可用于倾听者、回应、看法与角色，说明它已从纯粹的怜悯走出很远。

normal.en: The anatomical phrase sympathetic nervous system is fixed and technical, and should not be confused with the everyday sense.
normal.cn: 交感神经系统是固定的专业搭配，不应与日常义混淆。

normal.en: Unsympathetic is the negative, and it describes a person or a response that refuses to feel.
normal.cn: unsympathetic 是反义形式，形容拒绝去感受的人或回应。

normal.en: The adverb sympathetically tells how someone listened, spoke or looked.
normal.cn: 副词 sympathetically 说明某人如何倾听、说话或注视。

abstract.en: Picture a chair moved forward by half an arm's length, without any announcement.
abstract.cn: 想象一把椅子被往前挪了半臂的距离，没有任何说明。

abstract.en: Picture a folded note tucked into a letter of condolence.
abstract.cn: 想象一张折好的短笺夹在慰问信里。

abstract.en: Picture a nerve firing while the heart speeds up, two organs answering each other.
abstract.cn: 想象一条神经放电、心脏随之加速，两个器官彼此应答。

examples.en: The audience was sympathetic to the young speaker's nervousness.
examples.cn: 听众对年轻演讲者的紧张表示体谅。

examples.en: He is a sympathetic boss who listens before he decides.
examples.cn: 他是个体谅下属的上司，先听再决定。

examples.en: The drug acts on the sympathetic nervous system.
examples.cn: 这种药作用于交感神经系统。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「sym（相同）+ pathetic（感受）」——与受苦者有相同的感受 → 同情的、体谅的

root: 希腊 sympatheia（syn-「同」+ pathos「感受」）+ 形容词词尾 -etikos；由「相互感应」引申为「同情、赞同」。解剖学义来自旧生理学的「共感」观念。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one chair moved closer: feeling for pain, words for the bereaved, support for a cause, allowance for difficulty, a likeable manner, the answering nerve, two things in tune, and the character an audience pities.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一把被挪近的椅子展开：对痛苦的感受、写给丧家的话、对某种主张的支持、对困境的通融、讨人喜欢的举止、作出应答的神经、两相呼应的东西，以及观众所怜悯的角色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chair in a waiting room moved forward by half an arm's length.
core.cn: 核心意象：候诊室里一把被往前挪了半臂距离的椅子。

branches.en: FEELING AND ALLOWING: sorrow for another's pain, and a judgment that makes room for it.
branches.cn: 感受与容许：为他人痛苦而难过，以及为这份痛苦留出余地的判断。

branches.en: THE WORDS IN THE POST: condolence whose tone is marked by this adjective.
branches.cn: 寄出的话：语气由这个形容词标示的慰问。

branches.en: THE PAGE TAKES SIDES: a newspaper favourable to a strike or a demand.
branches.cn: 报纸选了边：对罢工或诉求表示赞同的报纸。

branches.en: EASY TO LIKE, EASY TO PITY: a pleasant neighbour, and a foolish character an audience feels for.
branches.cn: 讨人喜欢与令人同情：令人愉快的邻居，以及观众为其动情的愚蠢角色。

branches.en: ANSWERING ONE ANOTHER: the nerve that responds to stress, and two poems in tune.
branches.cn: 彼此应答：对应激作出反应的神经，以及语调相合的两首诗。

intro.en: Sympathetic is the adjective of sympathy, and its family runs from condolence to anatomy.
intro.cn: sympathetic 是 sympathy 的形容词，其词族从慰问一直延伸到解剖学。

latinIntro.en: Greek syn- 'with', pathos 'feeling' and the endings -eia, -etic, -ize, -er and -ally build the family. These are Greek elements, so no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 syn-「与」、pathos「感受」以及词尾 -eia、-etic、-ize、-er、-ally 构成这个词族。这些是希腊语构件，因此不列拉丁词条。

items.example: The prefix places the feeling alongside the sufferer.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把感受放在受苦者身旁。

items.example: The root supplies the emotional core.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供情感核心。

items.example: The Greek noun stands behind the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊名词是词族的来源。

items.example: The union expressed sympathy with the strikers.
items.exampleCN: 工会对罢工者表示同情。

items.example: The nurse was sympathetic when he described the pain.
items.exampleCN: 他描述疼痛时，护士表现出同情。

items.example: She spoke sympathetically about his loss.
items.exampleCN: 她同情地谈起他的损失。

items.example: The clerk was unsympathetic to the complaint.
items.exampleCN: 那名职员对投诉无动于衷。

items.example: He sympathized with the family's decision.
items.exampleCN: 他理解并赞同这家人的决定。

items.example: The cause attracted sympathizers in several countries.
items.exampleCN: 这项事业在数个国家吸引了同情者。
